the-strange.rule.ascendant-recursion-pot.blocked_reason: The described change is a world-level progression.

the-strange.rule.recursion-improvement-r.name: Recursion improvement ritual

effect.summary: Creators can spend XP through a ritual or process taking 1d6 hours to hasten maturity or add features.

the-strange.rule.recursion-improvement-r.cost_or_limit: XP expenditure is required; ritual or process takes 1d6 hours.
the-strange.rule.recursion-improvement-r.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure rather than a world mechanism.

the-strange.rule.hasten-maturity.name: Hasten maturity

effect.summary: Each XP spent by creators advances their recursion’s maturity by one month.

the-strange.rule.hasten-maturity.blocked_reason: The rule directly maps XP expenditure to elapsed maturation.

the-strange.rule.special-translation-zon.name: Special translation zone cost

effect.summary: Creators can spend 10 XP per zone level to restrict translation in a zone up to 100 feet across.

the-strange.rule.special-translation-zon.cost_or_limit: 10 XP per level; maximum zone diameter 100 feet.
the-strange.rule.special-translation-zon.combines: Higher-level restricted area within a recursion.
the-strange.rule.special-translation-zon.blocked_reason: A persistent zone that restricts translation requires an area-field effect.

the-strange.rule.time-and-space-cannot-b.name: Time and space cannot be altered in recursion creation

effect.summary: Creators cannot make a recursion infinitely large or make its time run faster or slower than linked worlds.

the-strange.rule.time-and-space-cannot-b.cost_or_limit: Size must stay within the stated guidelines; linked-world time is synchronized.
the-strange.rule.time-and-space-cannot-b.who_may: Recursion creators are subject to this restriction.
the-strange.rule.time-and-space-cannot-b.where_from: Earth, nearby dark-energy regions, and linked recursions
the-strange.rule.time-and-space-cannot-b.blocked_reason: Changing local time flow is explicitly prohibited and requires time manipulation beyond the basic grammar.

the-strange.rule.special-entry-translati.name: Special-entry translation zone

effect.summary: Creators can make a zone require a special condition, such as a pass phrase, key, or badge, for translation into it.

the-strange.rule.special-entry-translati.cost_or_limit: 10 XP per zone level; maximum diameter 100 feet.
the-strange.rule.special-entry-translati.blocked_reason: A persistent area-wide translation condition requires an area-field effect.

the-strange.rule.other-unique-recursion-.name: Other unique recursion features

effect.summary: A one-off immobile feature can generally be created for 10 XP per level of its effect.

the-strange.rule.other-unique-recursion-.cost_or_limit: 10 XP per level; the GM may reserve some effects for mature recursions.
the-strange.rule.other-unique-recursion-.combines: Recursion maturity may limit available features.
the-strange.rule.other-unique-recursion-.blocked_reason: The rule gives a cost for a feature without specifying an unimplementable effect.

the-strange.rule.resource-threshold.name: Resource threshold

effect.summary: A recursion below overall level 5 has no valuable resources in quantities worth collecting; a level-5 special area may contain a modest extractable deposit.

the-strange.rule.resource-threshold.cost_or_limit: A level-5 or higher unique area can support only a small deposit, not a fortune.
the-strange.rule.resource-threshold.blocked_reason: The resource threshold is a world rule.

the-strange.rule.native-inhabitants-and-.name: Native inhabitants and spark

effect.summary: Worthwhile native inhabitants do not appear before juvenile age; later inhabitants may follow creator-imposed dispositions, but some can gain the spark and choose their own path.

the-strange.rule.native-inhabitants-and-.go_wrong: A native may become independent of the creators’ intended purpose.
the-strange.rule.native-inhabitants-and-.who_may: Native inhabitants of a sufficiently mature recursion
the-strange.rule.native-inhabitants-and-.combines: Recursion age, creator design, and spark.
the-strange.rule.native-inhabitants-and-.blocked_reason: Creator-imposed predispositions and inhabitants’ independent will involve control of minds and agency.

the-strange.rule.native-level-ceiling.name: Native level ceiling

effect.summary: Most creatures and natives cannot exceed their recursion’s level, though a small number may.

the-strange.rule.native-level-ceiling.cost_or_limit: The ceiling applies to the bulk of the population, not every individual.
the-strange.rule.native-level-ceiling.who_may: Creatures and natives within a recursion
the-strange.rule.native-level-ceiling.blocked_reason: A population level limit is a straightforward rule.

the-strange.rule.earth-s-aleph-connectio.name: Earth’s Aleph connection

effect.summary: A buried Aleph component released a quantum field that uniquely connected Earth to the Strange and enabled many recursions and unusual beings.

the-strange.rule.earth-s-aleph-connectio.cost_or_limit: The component is buried beneath Earth’s mantle; its existence is unknown to the named groups.
the-strange.rule.earth-s-aleph-connectio.go_wrong: The original device malfunctioned and shattered.
the-strange.rule.earth-s-aleph-connectio.who_may: Earth and its living inhabitants are affected.
the-strange.rule.earth-s-aleph-connectio.where_from: A fragment of the alien system Aleph
the-strange.rule.earth-s-aleph-connectio.combines: Fictional leakage, paradoxes, spinners, and vectors.
the-strange.rule.earth-s-aleph-connectio.blocked_reason: The setting-wide connection is a persistent interaction between worlds and multiple phenomena.

the-strange.rule.translating-out-of-a-ce.name: Translating out of a cell in Holding

effect.summary: Leaving a Holding cell by translation requires a difficulty 9 roll.

the-strange.rule.translating-out-of-a-ce.who_may: A person attempting to translate from a cell
the-strange.rule.translating-out-of-a-ce.blocked_reason: A translation difficulty can be represented as a basic movement limit.

the-strange.rule.butterfly-theory-of-tra.name: Butterfly theory of translation

effect.summary: The theory claims a translator dies and a copy made from local material continues in the new recursion.

the-strange.rule.butterfly-theory-of-tra.cost_or_limit: Claimed to occur with each translation.
the-strange.rule.butterfly-theory-of-tra.go_wrong: The original person is claimed to die.
the-strange.rule.butterfly-theory-of-tra.mind: The copy retains the former person’s identity, according to the theory.
the-strange.rule.butterfly-theory-of-tra.who_may: People who translate, according to the theory
the-strange.rule.butterfly-theory-of-tra.combines: Explains the Butterfly Objectors’ rejection of translation.
the-strange.rule.butterfly-theory-of-tra.blocked_reason: Death and continuation as a copy require modeling identity and soul state beyond basic effects.

the-strange.rule.law-of-psionics.name: Law of Psionics

effect.summary: Atom Nocturne operates under a law that supports psychic abilities.

the-strange.rule.law-of-psionics.cost_or_limit: Imported psychic Talent is strained by Earth’s alternative law.
the-strange.rule.law-of-psionics.go_wrong: Psychic abilities may be depleted or become dangerous outside their home recursion.
the-strange.rule.law-of-psionics.who_may: Creatures and powers in Atom Nocturne
the-strange.rule.law-of-psionics.combines: Interacts adversely with Earth’s law when Soma translates there.
the-strange.rule.law-of-psionics.blocked_reason: The law’s interaction with and degradation of a power needs a power-interaction mechanic.

the-strange.rule.law-of-standard-physics.name: Law of Standard Physics

effect.summary: Earth and Truetopia operate under ordinary physics, which constrains artifacts and powers.

the-strange.rule.law-of-standard-physics.cost_or_limit: Many artifacts from other recursions cannot translate to Earth.
the-strange.rule.law-of-standard-physics.go_wrong: Imported creatures may disintegrate under Earth’s natural laws.
the-strange.rule.law-of-standard-physics.combines: Contrasts with other recursion laws and affects imported beings and artifacts.
the-strange.rule.law-of-standard-physics.blocked_reason: The law’s effects on imported powers, artifacts, and beings require cross-system interactions.

the-strange.rule.homebound-translation-r.name: Homebound translation restriction

effect.summary: Translating into or out of Homebound requires a difficulty 10 Intellect-based task.

the-strange.rule.homebound-translation-r.cost_or_limit: Difficulty 10; a translation gate is the only reliable route.
the-strange.rule.homebound-translation-r.go_wrong: A failed attempt may leave a traveler unable to enter or exit.
the-strange.rule.homebound-translation-r.who_may: Anyone attempting translation to or from Homebound
the-strange.rule.homebound-translation-r.combines: OSR maintains a gate on a moving rail car.
the-strange.rule.homebound-translation-r.blocked_reason: A translation difficulty can be represented as a basic movement limit.

the-strange.rule.law-of-magic.name: Law of Magic

effect.summary: Ardeyn operates under a law of magic.

the-strange.rule.law-of-magic.blocked_reason: The passage names the law but does not describe a specific effect that exceeds the basic grammar.

the-strange.rule.seven-rules.name: Seven Rules

effect.summary: Fence dangerous Strange creatures out of Ardeyn, though some breach the boundary.

the-strange.rule.seven-rules.go_wrong: Some creatures find a way inside.

the-strange.rule.ardeyn-calendar.name: Ardeyn calendar

effect.summary: Counts years from the Maker’s betrayal, and measures a 396-day year in seasons and months.

the-strange.rule.ardeyn-calendar.cost_or_limit: The betrayal’s date is only roughly reckoned as a thousand years ago.
the-strange.rule.ardeyn-calendar.combines: Weather and cycles in the Strange inform the calendar.

the-strange.rule.netters-claim.name: netters’ claim

effect.summary: A netter may claim a particular stretch of the falls only while their nets remain unbroken.

the-strange.rule.netters-claim.cost_or_limit: A broken net ends the claim.

the-strange.rule.red-pact.name: Red Pact

effect.summary: Keeps dragons out of the Citadel except during the Harrowing, when they are confined to its arena.

the-strange.rule.red-pact.cost_or_limit: The exception lasts two weeks in Suntide and requires a dragon to bring a worthy hoard prize.
the-strange.rule.red-pact.who_may: Dragons are subject to the pact.
the-strange.rule.red-pact.blocked_reason: The pact imposes a location-specific restriction on dragons.

the-strange.rule.harrowing-contest-outco.name: Harrowing contest outcome

effect.summary: A winning dragon may take survivors as slaves or eat them and claim their gear; winning mortals take the dragon's prize.

the-strange.rule.harrowing-contest-outco.cost_or_limit: The contest uses loose engagement rules and a team of four mortals.

the-strange.rule.ardeyn-s-cliff-fall.name: Ardeyn's cliff fall

effect.summary: Falling from Ardeyn's upper cliff faces usually leads to impact on a lower, shallower slope rather than directly into the Strange.

the-strange.rule.ardeyn-s-cliff-fall.cost_or_limit: The slope reverses at a termination line about 50 miles down; passing that lip sends objects into the Strange.
the-strange.rule.ardeyn-s-cliff-fall.go_wrong: A fall can smash the falling person or object.
the-strange.rule.ardeyn-s-cliff-fall.combines: The termination zone allows steep-slope navigation.

the-strange.rule.borderlands-weather.name: Borderlands weather

effect.summary: Temperatures can plunge or spike rapidly, while powerful winds can form tornadoes.

the-strange.rule.borderlands-weather.go_wrong: Exposure risks blizzards, sunstroke, or being swept away.
the-strange.rule.borderlands-weather.who_may: People and unsecured structures in the Borderlands
the-strange.rule.borderlands-weather.blocked_reason: The variable weather affects broad areas and is not represented by a single basic effect.

the-strange.rule.translation-gate-access.name: Translation gate access

effect.summary: The September Embassy gate accepts only travelers bearing the Traitor's Crown tattoo.

the-strange.rule.translation-gate-access.go_wrong: Unauthorized travelers cannot use the gate.
the-strange.rule.translation-gate-access.combines: The gate provides translation to the office.
the-strange.rule.translation-gate-access.blocked_reason: The gate restricts passage by a credential.

the-strange.rule.ardeyn-death-and-the-ni.name: Ardeyn death and the Night Vault

effect.summary: Creatures slain in Ardeyn may persist as spirits and enter the Night Vault, unlike those dying in other recursions or the Strange.

the-strange.rule.ardeyn-death-and-the-ni.cost_or_limit: Travelers arriving through an inapposite gate do not have souls descend there.
the-strange.rule.ardeyn-death-and-the-ni.go_wrong: Spirits may be devoured, transformed, or judged into other fates.
the-strange.rule.ardeyn-death-and-the-ni.mind: The spirit remains a continuing entity.
the-strange.rule.ardeyn-death-and-the-ni.who_may: Creatures slain in Ardeyn, subject to the stated exceptions
the-strange.rule.ardeyn-death-and-the-ni.combines: Court of Sleep can judge and rescue spirits.
the-strange.rule.ardeyn-death-and-the-ni.blocked_reason: The rule defines which deaths produce persistent spirits and their afterlife path.

the-strange.rule.spirit-pool-magic.name: Spirit pool magic

effect.summary: A trained user adjacent to a spirit pool may teleport between pools visited before and improve a roll by three steps.

the-strange.rule.spirit-pool-magic.cost_or_limit: Requires adjacency to a pool and training in its magic.
the-strange.rule.spirit-pool-magic.go_wrong: Pools are hard to find and lie in dangerous places.
the-strange.rule.spirit-pool-magic.who_may: People trained in spirit pool magic
the-strange.rule.spirit-pool-magic.combines: Provides both teleportation and roll enhancement.
the-strange.rule.spirit-pool-magic.blocked_reason: Teleportation between previously visited locations requires spatial destination tracking.

the-strange.rule.cursed-soul-weapon-depl.name: Cursed Soul Weapon depletion

effect.summary: When a cursed soul weapon depletes, it demands a replacement soul; without killing the nearest sentient creature, the wielder's soul is forfeit.

the-strange.rule.cursed-soul-weapon-depl.go_wrong: The wielder loses her soul if she fails to kill the nearest sentient creature.
the-strange.rule.cursed-soul-weapon-depl.blocked_reason: It transfers and forfeits souls, which the basic effect grammar cannot model.

the-strange.rule.ruk-s-movement-through-.name: Ruk’s movement through the Strange

effect.summary: Ruk could travel through informational canals by continually rewriting the laws governing the Strange.

the-strange.rule.ruk-s-movement-through-.cost_or_limit: Ruk’s movement was stopped by properties of a nearby world.
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-movement-through-.go_wrong: Damage and disruption eventually left Ruk stranded.
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-movement-through-.who_may: Ruk’s builders or governing recursion mechanism
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-movement-through-.where_from: Ruk’s nature as a mobile recursion
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-movement-through-.combines: Its movement ended when it ran aground near Earth.
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-movement-through-.mechanism: Recursion movement by rewriting local laws
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-movement-through-.blocked_reason: The passage describes a world mechanism without an effect outside the basic grammar.

the-strange.rule.the-all-song-runs-throu.name: The All Song runs through engineered tissue

effect.summary: The network lets Ruk natives store information and communicate across great distances.

the-strange.rule.the-all-song-runs-throu.cost_or_limit: Direct use is easier with an umbilical.
the-strange.rule.the-all-song-runs-throu.go_wrong: Some fear it is eroding Ruk’s connection to its heritage.
the-strange.rule.the-all-song-runs-throu.mind: Connection can produce overwhelming sensory experiences.
the-strange.rule.the-all-song-runs-throu.who_may: Ruk natives have a minor connection; others can use suitable interfaces.
the-strange.rule.the-all-song-runs-throu.where_from: The All Song’s presence in engineered Ruk tissue
the-strange.rule.the-all-song-runs-throu.blocked_reason: The stated storage and communication functions are representable through information effects.

the-strange.rule.ruk-s-edge-growth.name: Ruk’s edge growth

effect.summary: The Periphery grows as an organic extension of Ruk.

the-strange.rule.ruk-s-edge-growth.cost_or_limit: Growth varies from about a centimeter to a meter or more per day.
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-edge-growth.combines: The region’s growth has accelerated in recent centuries.
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-edge-growth.blocked_reason: The stated setting change can be represented as a continuing world condition.

the-strange.rule.communion-with-the-true.name: Communion with the True Code

effect.summary: Eating communion grants an asset on a related Intellect task performed within an hour.

the-strange.rule.communion-with-the-true.cost_or_limit: Benefit applies to a True Code-related Intellect task within one hour.
the-strange.rule.communion-with-the-true.who_may: Church apostles and others taking communion
the-strange.rule.communion-with-the-true.where_from: A wafer synthesized from the True Code
the-strange.rule.communion-with-the-true.combines: Communion from First Apostle Ah-kalla provides greater advantages via the True Code platter.
the-strange.rule.communion-with-the-true.blocked_reason: The stated temporary task advantage can be represented as a basic effect.

the-strange.rule.quiet-cabal-mission-enh.name: Quiet Cabal mission enhancement rule

effect.summary: A Cabal agent may receive one temporary enhancement as an asset to one task for a mission.

the-strange.rule.quiet-cabal-mission-enh.cost_or_limit: One object per mission; it must be returned intact when the mission ends.
the-strange.rule.quiet-cabal-mission-enh.go_wrong: Failure to return it intact violates the stated expectation.
the-strange.rule.quiet-cabal-mission-enh.who_may: Quiet Cabal agents requesting mission kits
the-strange.rule.quiet-cabal-mission-enh.where_from: The Outfitting level of High Command
the-strange.rule.quiet-cabal-mission-enh.combines: Enhancement may be a pod, bioengineered spine, or another temporary bodily addition.
the-strange.rule.quiet-cabal-mission-enh.blocked_reason: It assigns a temporary enhancement with a mission-bound duration and return condition.

the-strange.rule.genetic-profiles-and-id.name: Genetic profiles and identity

effect.summary: A complete genetic profile is treated as a piece of its subject's soul and can enable tailored poisons or parasites.

the-strange.rule.genetic-profiles-and-id.cost_or_limit: Profiles are prohibited by Ruk law and sensibilities.
the-strange.rule.genetic-profiles-and-id.go_wrong: Possession can enable person-specific harm and coercion.
the-strange.rule.genetic-profiles-and-id.who_may: Profile holders can exploit the information.
the-strange.rule.genetic-profiles-and-id.combines: Genome, epigenetic factors, and microbiome code.
the-strange.rule.genetic-profiles-and-id.blocked_reason: The profile is explicitly treated as part of a person's soul, which the basic effect grammar cannot model.

the-strange.rule.ruk-s-true-code-disrupt.name: Ruk's True Code disruption

effect.summary: An apocalyptic encounter in the Strange disrupted the True Code, producing the All Song and Ruk's divisions.

the-strange.rule.ruk-s-true-code-disrupt.cost_or_limit: The event's nature and cause remain uncertain.
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-true-code-disrupt.mind: The disruption gave rise to the All Song.
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-true-code-disrupt.combines: Associated with the Qinod and the later Qinod Singularity.
the-strange.rule.ruk-s-true-code-disrupt.blocked_reason: The cause and operation of the code disruption are unknown.

the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-behav.name: Qinod Singularity behavior

effect.summary: The Singularity manifests randomly, ejecting objects and sometimes destructive animate constructs.

the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-behav.go_wrong: Constructs commonly attack life and structures.
the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-behav.combines: Some ejected devices function as artifacts.
the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-behav.blocked_reason: The random manifestation and varied contents cannot be run as a single defined basic effect.

the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-entry.name: Qinod Singularity entry attempts

effect.summary: Those attempting to enter its maw have been killed before crossing or have disappeared.

the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-entry.cost_or_limit: Three known attempts ended this way.
the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-entry.go_wrong: Entrants are fried or do not return.
the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-entry.who_may: Anyone attempting entry is at risk.
the-strange.rule.qinod-singularity-entry.blocked_reason: The threshold's exact lethal or transport mechanism is unspecified.

the-strange.rule.travel-laws-in-the-stra.name: Travel laws in the Strange

effect.summary: Visitors carry a thin film of their most recent recursion's laws; they cannot normally translate directly into the Strange.

the-strange.rule.travel-laws-in-the-stra.cost_or_limit: No playable races or foci are offered on first entry.
the-strange.rule.travel-laws-in-the-stra.go_wrong: Travel may be dangerous and psychologically harmful.
the-strange.rule.travel-laws-in-the-stra.mind: Different regions may affect a traveler's psyche.
the-strange.rule.travel-laws-in-the-stra.blocked_reason: The described restriction and carryover can be represented as world rules.

the-strange.rule.chaosphere-surfing-move.name: Chaosphere surfing movement

effect.summary: Surfing a fractal wave gives long-range movement each round; transit to a known site takes its listed time.

the-strange.rule.chaosphere-surfing-move.cost_or_limit: Travel is Intellect- or Speed-task dependent; halving transit time increases difficulty.
the-strange.rule.chaosphere-surfing-move.go_wrong: Failed transit can leave the traveler lost; failure while lost raises alienation.
the-strange.rule.chaosphere-surfing-move.who_may: Travelers who can navigate or surf the Strange.
the-strange.rule.chaosphere-surfing-move.combines: Beacons, signposts, and known sites guide travel.
the-strange.rule.chaosphere-surfing-move.blocked_reason: The alienation penalty accumulates and is reduced through successful reorientation, a persistent state not covered by the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.recursion-interface.name: Recursion interface

effect.summary: A recursion permeable to the Strange appears as a small translucent bubble, with interface size adjusted to the recursion.

the-strange.rule.recursion-interface.cost_or_limit: Exterior is usually no more than a few miles across and may shrink to about ten feet.
the-strange.rule.recursion-interface.go_wrong: Finding an entry point may be difficult.
the-strange.rule.recursion-interface.combines: Recursions directly connected to each other may also provide access.
the-strange.rule.recursion-interface.blocked_reason: The described access boundary can be recorded as a world rule.

the-strange.rule.recursion-entry-and-mat.name: Recursion entry and material adaptation

effect.summary: Strange materials can enter recursions and adapt enough to exist in their context.

the-strange.rule.recursion-entry-and-mat.cost_or_limit: Native creatures are barred unless they trick the interface or a native opens a way.
the-strange.rule.recursion-entry-and-mat.go_wrong: Strange materials may lose properties in another context, such as dust no longer glowing on Earth.
the-strange.rule.recursion-entry-and-mat.who_may: Travelers and materials can enter; native creatures face the stated restriction.
the-strange.rule.recursion-entry-and-mat.combines: Inapposite gates and translation can admit travelers or cyphers.
the-strange.rule.recursion-entry-and-mat.blocked_reason: The entry restriction and material adaptation are describable as ordinary changes and access limits.

the-strange.rule.alienation.name: Alienation

effect.summary: Strange exposure accumulates alienation, which harms stat Pools and may cause dementia.

the-strange.rule.alienation.cost_or_limit: Each factor damages all three stat Pools when the factor rises and after a qualifying eight-hour rest; breaks and finding one’s way can reduce factors, while training provides a buffer.
the-strange.rule.alienation.go_wrong: Impairment or debilitation may lead to a dementia fit that raises task difficulty briefly.
the-strange.rule.alienation.mind: Can cause temporary dementia after alienation-related impairment or debilitation.
the-strange.rule.alienation.who_may: Creatures not native to the Strange gain alienation when exposed.
the-strange.rule.alienation.where_from: Direct exposure to the Strange and specified events.
the-strange.rule.alienation.combines: Strange-related skills buffer exposure; shelter and rest reduce factors.
the-strange.rule.alienation.mechanism: accumulating exposure track with recurring damage
the-strange.rule.alienation.blocked_reason: The rule requires an accumulating factor track that triggers repeated stat damage and may produce a separate mental consequence.

the-strange.rule.recursion-growth-throug.name: Recursion growth through self-awareness

effect.summary: A recursion may grow to accommodate inhabitants who become conscious.

the-strange.rule.recursion-growth-throug.cost_or_limit: Growth is likely when enough inhabitants gain self-awareness.
the-strange.rule.recursion-growth-throug.who_may: Applies to recursions with developing conscious inhabitants.
the-strange.rule.recursion-growth-throug.blocked_reason: The rule describes a world change without a missing effect capability.

the-strange.rule.entropic-seed-recovery.name: Entropic seed recovery

effect.summary: Recursion rules damaged by an entropic seed recover slowly.

the-strange.rule.entropic-seed-recovery.cost_or_limit: Recovery takes a long time; no duration is given.
the-strange.rule.entropic-seed-recovery.go_wrong: The affected recursion may be ruined before recovery.
the-strange.rule.entropic-seed-recovery.who_may: Applies to recursions damaged by a seed.
the-strange.rule.entropic-seed-recovery.combines: A seed may affect connected recursions or a prime world.
the-strange.rule.entropic-seed-recovery.blocked_reason: The passage states a slow recovery limit without specifying a mechanic that is unavailable.

the-strange.rule.the-dark-energy-network.name: The dark energy network and the Precursors

effect.summary: The original network copied a traveler’s state to a destination, but malfunctioned and began trapping users.

the-strange.rule.the-dark-energy-network.cost_or_limit: Travel adapts the new instance to local conditions.
the-strange.rule.the-dark-energy-network.go_wrong: The malfunctioning network traps travelers instead of transporting them.
the-strange.rule.the-dark-energy-network.mind: The traveler’s state is copied; the passage does not explain its mental continuity.
the-strange.rule.the-dark-energy-network.who_may: Users of the ancient transit network.
the-strange.rule.the-dark-energy-network.where_from: Built by the Precursors; now the Strange.
the-strange.rule.the-dark-energy-network.combines: Uses state upload, routing, and printing at a distant location.
the-strange.rule.the-dark-energy-network.blocked_reason: The rule depends on the identity and continuity of a copied traveler’s state.

the-strange.rule.network-ping-and-planet.name: Network ping and planetovore danger

effect.summary: Advanced civilizations connecting to the Strange draw planetovores’ attention to their worlds.

the-strange.rule.network-ping-and-planet.cost_or_limit: Unshielded prime worlds are almost always consumed.
the-strange.rule.network-ping-and-planet.go_wrong: A world becomes vulnerable to planetovores.
the-strange.rule.network-ping-and-planet.who_may: Civilizations that connect to the network.
the-strange.rule.network-ping-and-planet.where_from: The Strange and its surrounding recursions.
the-strange.rule.network-ping-and-planet.combines: Recursions can shield a prime world from direct exposure.
the-strange.rule.network-ping-and-planet.blocked_reason: The connection-triggered attention and danger can be represented as a world rule.

the-strange.rule.the-luminous-circuit-s-.name: The Luminous Circuit’s travel and hazard

effect.summary: Riders can be carried along the current; unprotected contact can turn a creature into solid fundament.

the-strange.rule.the-luminous-circuit-s-.cost_or_limit: Travel time resembles self-powered surfing; a craft halves it; the full circuit takes decades.
the-strange.rule.the-luminous-circuit-s-.go_wrong: A difficulty-four Might defense failure transforms a creature into fundament.
the-strange.rule.the-luminous-circuit-s-.who_may: Travelers who ride the current; contact is dangerous without a craft.
the-strange.rule.the-luminous-circuit-s-.combines: A fractal surf wing or chaos skiff halves travel time.
the-strange.rule.the-luminous-circuit-s-.blocked_reason: The current can permanently turn a creature into solid fundament.

the-strange.rule.home-recursion-film.name: Home-recursion film

effect.summary: Travelers carry a thin film of their home recursion that prevents passive environmental threats from harming them.

the-strange.rule.home-recursion-film.combines: Explains why Malathamashawi's clear blood does not drown explorers.
the-strange.rule.home-recursion-film.blocked_reason: It is a passive protective rule.

the-strange.rule.strange-artifact-transl.name: Strange artifact translation

effect.summary: Artifacts forged in the Strange continue working in other recursions and may adapt their form to fit the new context.

the-strange.rule.strange-artifact-transl.cost_or_limit: Applies to artifacts forged within the Strange.
the-strange.rule.strange-artifact-transl.combines: Some adapt in a manner like cyphers.
the-strange.rule.strange-artifact-transl.blocked_reason: The rule changes an item's contextual form and operation.

the-strange.rule.crow-coin-drains-creatu.name: Crow coin drains creature essence

effect.summary: Crow coin represents essence and health; losing enough can kill its source.

the-strange.rule.crow-coin-drains-creatu.cost_or_limit: Recovery can prevent death; PCs recover points normally.
the-strange.rule.crow-coin-drains-creatu.who_may: Applies to creatures whose essence is taken as coin.
the-strange.rule.crow-coin-drains-creatu.combines: A handshake and verbal agreement can seal payment.
the-strange.rule.crow-coin-drains-creatu.blocked_reason: The rule makes currency a transferable portion of a creature’s essence.

the-strange.rule.nanovirus-infestation.name: Nanovirus infestation

effect.summary: Exposure leaves permanent quiescent particles that can awaken after a failed Might defense.

the-strange.rule.nanovirus-infestation.cost_or_limit: Daily defense in the Graveyard; after awakening, a difficulty-3 defense each round.
the-strange.rule.nanovirus-infestation.go_wrong: Failure causes 3 ambient damage each round until the virus is killed or the victim dies; the corpse becomes silicone.
the-strange.rule.nanovirus-infestation.who_may: Any creature entering the Graveyard; sacrosancts roll yearly instead of daily.
the-strange.rule.nanovirus-infestation.combines: Translating to another recursion can destroy particles or end the infection.
the-strange.rule.nanovirus-infestation.mechanism: Latent infection, escalating checks, and damage
the-strange.rule.nanovirus-infestation.blocked_reason: The disease escalates from daily to per-round checks and can permanently transform a corpse.

the-strange.rule.homunculi-share-the-bet.name: Homunculi share the Betrayer’s soul

effect.summary: The Betrayer can create only a limited number of homunculi because they receive fragments of his finite soul.

the-strange.rule.homunculi-share-the-bet.cost_or_limit: His mortal soul permits several hundred greens, about a hundred reds, and only a handful of clears.
the-strange.rule.homunculi-share-the-bet.mind: Soul fragments determine the homunculi’s awareness and competence.
the-strange.rule.homunculi-share-the-bet.combines: The Vats and a remnant of the Betrayer’s former power enable the process.
the-strange.rule.homunculi-share-the-bet.blocked_reason: It requires a model for dividing and allocating a soul among multiple bodies.

the-strange.rule.native-abilities-persis.name: Native abilities persist under matching laws

effect.summary: A non-native creature retains its full abilities in a recursion operating under the same law as its origin, and every creature retains them in the Strange.

the-strange.rule.native-abilities-persis.cost_or_limit: Outside those conditions, the passage does not guarantee full abilities.
the-strange.rule.native-abilities-persis.combines: Applies to travel through gates or other transfers.

the-strange.rule.hydra-head-acquisition.name: hydra head acquisition

effect.summary: A hydra that kills a human gains the victim’s head and recovers health on the next round.

the-strange.rule.hydra-head-acquisition.cost_or_limit: The head is gained on the following round and can act only verbally or mentally.
the-strange.rule.hydra-head-acquisition.combines: The hydra gains 5 health and may use the head’s remaining abilities.
the-strange.rule.hydra-head-acquisition.blocked_reason: It preserves aspects of a dead person’s mind and incorporates them into a creature.

the-strange.rule.kray-entry-into-ardeyn.name: Kray entry into Ardeyn

effect.summary: Kray can bypass the Seven Rules through the Betrayer’s aid, while seedlings usually need a native to bring them into a recursion.

the-strange.rule.kray-entry-into-ardeyn.cost_or_limit: Seedlings that enter may drift until they find a living host.
the-strange.rule.kray-entry-into-ardeyn.go_wrong: A host may be hollowed out and used for gestation.
the-strange.rule.kray-entry-into-ardeyn.mind: A scurrier can impersonate its host before emerging.
the-strange.rule.kray-entry-into-ardeyn.who_may: Kray, with the usual assistance of a recursion native.
the-strange.rule.kray-entry-into-ardeyn.combines: Seedlings need a living creature as fertile ground.
the-strange.rule.kray-entry-into-ardeyn.blocked_reason: The rule describes exceptions to the setting’s barriers between recursions.

the-strange.rule.kray-web-cocooning.name: Kray web cocooning

effect.summary: A dead victim cocooned in kray webbing is deleted from Ardeyn or changed into another form.

the-strange.rule.kray-web-cocooning.cost_or_limit: The result is revealed if the cocoon is scraped away.
the-strange.rule.kray-web-cocooning.go_wrong: Victims may become slime, stone, or a swarm of scurriers.
the-strange.rule.kray-web-cocooning.combines: Kray drones use web attacks to cocoon targets.
the-strange.rule.kray-web-cocooning.blocked_reason: The rule permits a victim’s form to be radically changed or erased.

the-strange.rule.kro-courser-leash.name: kro courser leash

effect.summary: A leash gives its holder control over an associated courser or pack.

the-strange.rule.kro-courser-leash.cost_or_limit: Destroying the leash makes the associated courser or pack attack nearby creatures without restraint.
the-strange.rule.kro-courser-leash.go_wrong: The loss of the leash causes uncontrolled attacks.
the-strange.rule.kro-courser-leash.mind: The leash directs the courser’s behavior.
the-strange.rule.kro-courser-leash.combines: Created alongside the courser by the same magic.
the-strange.rule.kro-courser-leash.blocked_reason: The leash binds a creature’s actions to its holder.

the-strange.rule.myriand-volunteer-trans.name: Myriand volunteer transformation

effect.summary: A biological pod changes a volunteer into a battle chrysalid and suppresses their former identity during service.

the-strange.rule.myriand-volunteer-trans.cost_or_limit: Activation occurs on patrol shifts or remotely for specific missions.
the-strange.rule.myriand-volunteer-trans.go_wrong: The transformed volunteer loses their former identity and obeys the law rigidly.
the-strange.rule.myriand-volunteer-trans.mind: Personality and identity change during the transformation.
the-strange.rule.myriand-volunteer-trans.combines: The pod is fused to the volunteer’s body.
the-strange.rule.myriand-volunteer-trans.blocked_reason: The mechanism transforms both body and mind.

the-strange.rule.all-song-security-layer.name: All Song security layer

effect.summary: A Myriand veteran uses a shared layer to induce regret and surrender in selected nearby creatures.

the-strange.rule.all-song-security-layer.cost_or_limit: Targets may resist again each round; the effect lasts up to one minute.
the-strange.rule.all-song-security-layer.go_wrong: An OFFENDER tag may instead mark a target and remain for three days.
the-strange.rule.all-song-security-layer.mind: The effect alters emotions and willingness to defend oneself.
the-strange.rule.all-song-security-layer.who_may: Myriand veterans can access the security layer.
the-strange.rule.all-song-security-layer.combines: All Ruk creatures and PCs translated to Ruk are connected to the All Song.
the-strange.rule.all-song-security-layer.blocked_reason: It uses a shared network to exert sustained emotional and behavioral control.

the-strange.rule.non-magic-trail-breakin.name: non-Magic trail breaking

effect.summary: A kro courser loses a quickened creature’s scent trail if the target enters a recursion that does not operate under Magic.

the-strange.rule.non-magic-trail-breakin.cost_or_limit: The trail must be less than a week old to be followed in the first place.
the-strange.rule.non-magic-trail-breakin.go_wrong: The trail is broken by travel through a non-Magic recursion or Earth.
the-strange.rule.non-magic-trail-breakin.combines: Kro coursers can otherwise follow quickened creatures through recursions.
the-strange.rule.non-magic-trail-breakin.blocked_reason: The limit can be represented as a restriction on tracking.

the-strange.rule.crow-coin-and-courser-c.name: crow coin and courser creation

effect.summary: Creating a kro courser requires three chests of crow coin, a mystic recipe, and organizational approval.

the-strange.rule.crow-coin-and-courser-c.cost_or_limit: The stated material and approval requirements must be met.
the-strange.rule.crow-coin-and-courser-c.go_wrong: The resulting creature decays without magical maintenance.
the-strange.rule.crow-coin-and-courser-c.combines: Requires a recently deceased kro corpse and creates a leash with the courser.
the-strange.rule.crow-coin-and-courser-c.blocked_reason: The leash and courser’s magical control depend on a crafted, bound magical effect.

the-strange.rule.myriand-sentencing-auth.name: myriand sentencing authority

effect.summary: Myriand veterans may judge and sentence lawbreakers when time or circumstances demand it.

the-strange.rule.myriand-sentencing-auth.cost_or_limit: Otherwise, they return suspects to faction headquarters for processing.
the-strange.rule.myriand-sentencing-auth.blocked_reason: This is a procedural legal authority, not a supernatural effect.

the-strange.rule.soulshorn-return-after-.name: Soulshorn return after death

effect.summary: A slain soulshorn revives at full health after seven days unless its remains are burned before then.

the-strange.rule.soulshorn-return-after-.cost_or_limit: Burning the remains prevents the return.
the-strange.rule.soulshorn-return-after-.blocked_reason: This rule requires persistent soul/death state and a timed return.

the-strange.rule.wrath-mind-erosion.name: Wrath mind erosion

effect.summary: A spirit’s mind deteriorates over time without physical substance to renew it.

the-strange.rule.wrath-mind-erosion.cost_or_limit: The decline occurs over time and may eventually leave the spirit nearly mindless.
the-strange.rule.wrath-mind-erosion.go_wrong: The spirit becomes destructive and loses its former identity.
the-strange.rule.wrath-mind-erosion.mind: Progressive loss of memory and reason.
the-strange.rule.wrath-mind-erosion.blocked_reason: The rule depends on a dead spirit persisting and changing mentally over time.

the-strange.rule.cyphers-are-one-use-ite.name: Cyphers are one-use items

effect.summary: Cyphers are consumed when activated.

the-strange.rule.cyphers-are-one-use-ite.blocked_reason: A consumable item rule is representable.

the-strange.rule.cypher-limit.name: Cypher limit

effect.summary: Excess cyphers vanish until the possessor is at their maximum, and cannot be recovered.

the-strange.rule.cypher-limit.cost_or_limit: Each character has a maximum number of cyphers
the-strange.rule.cypher-limit.go_wrong: Excess items disappear and return to the Strange
the-strange.rule.cypher-limit.combines: Occultic cyphers count as two toward the limit
the-strange.rule.cypher-limit.blocked_reason: The rule removes excess items from possession and sends them elsewhere.

the-strange.rule.occultic-cyphers-count-.name: Occultic cyphers count as two

effect.summary: A complex occultic cypher uses two spaces in the carrying limit.

the-strange.rule.occultic-cyphers-count-.combines: Applies to the cypher possession limit

the-strange.rule.cyphers-change-form-acr.name: Cyphers change form across recursions

effect.summary: A cypher takes a context-appropriate appearance in each recursion while retaining its function.

the-strange.rule.cyphers-change-form-acr.blocked_reason: The rule changes an item’s form while preserving its effect.

the-strange.rule.recursion-code-use.name: Recursion code use

effect.summary: A recursion code redirects a successful translation but does not create its gate; use expends or disables the code.

the-strange.rule.recursion-code-use.go_wrong: The code dissipates or loses its cypher-like ability.
the-strange.rule.recursion-code-use.blocked_reason: This rule describes a consumable effect that can be represented with the basic grammar.

the-strange.rule.sheltering-recursion-pe.name: Sheltering recursion permanence

effect.summary: A created pocket recursion remains permanent even after its device becomes inactive.

the-strange.rule.sheltering-recursion-pe.cost_or_limit: Created recursion is pocket-dimension sized and follows the host recursion's law.
the-strange.rule.sheltering-recursion-pe.blocked_reason: The rule requires a persistent, separately accessible dimension.

the-strange.rule.stasis-preservation.name: Stasis preservation

effect.summary: A subject in stasis does not age and emerges alive in its original condition, without memory of the inactive period.

the-strange.rule.stasis-preservation.cost_or_limit: Stasis lasts for the cypher-level number of days or until violently disturbed.
the-strange.rule.stasis-preservation.go_wrong: The subject has no memory of the interval.
the-strange.rule.stasis-preservation.mind: Removes memory of time spent inactive.
the-strange.rule.stasis-preservation.blocked_reason: The rule requires time suspension and a specified preserved state.

effect.summary: A recursion is strange and unfamiliar rather than simply a parallel version of a familiar location.

the-strange.rule.translation-changes-the.name: Translation changes the traveler's body, gear, and focus

effect.summary: On translating, characters arrive with new bodies, gear, and foci.

the-strange.rule.translation-changes-the.combines: Changes body, equipment, and focus together.
the-strange.rule.translation-changes-the.blocked_reason: The passage says translation changes a character's form and carried equipment, which exceeds the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.character-death-ends-th.name: Character death ends the character's play unless a survival is allowed

effect.summary: Death normally removes the character from play, though the GM may allow a near-death survival with lasting drawbacks.

the-strange.rule.character-death-ends-th.cost_or_limit: A permitted survival carries an injury, weakness, inability, or other drawback.
the-strange.rule.character-death-ends-th.go_wrong: The character may die; survival can leave lasting injuries or limitations.
the-strange.rule.character-death-ends-th.combines: Companions or luck may save a character at the brink of death.
the-strange.rule.character-death-ends-th.blocked_reason: The passage defines character death and an exceptional survival state, which requires tracking a character's continued existence.

the-strange.rule.cypher-recognition.name: Cypher recognition

effect.summary: Quickened characters can sense a cypher by handling it, but identifying its exact effect takes a knowledge roll.

the-strange.rule.cypher-recognition.cost_or_limit: Naive characters need context or experimentation to identify items readily
the-strange.rule.cypher-recognition.blocked_reason: Recognizing an item’s nature and determining its exact effect require an information-sensing capability beyond the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.naive-characters-and-st.name: Naive characters and starting cyphers

effect.summary: Naive characters generally start without cyphers, though they may unknowingly possess one.

the-strange.rule.naive-characters-and-st.cost_or_limit: Finding cyphers is normally part of their awakening
the-strange.rule.naive-characters-and-st.mind: A character may get a vague feeling when handling one
the-strange.rule.naive-characters-and-st.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward restriction on initial possession.

the-strange.rule.translation-versus-goin.name: Translation versus going through a gate

effect.summary: Translation integrates travelers into a recursion, while an inapposite gate provides no local information and does not translate their gear or abilities.

the-strange.rule.translation-versus-goin.cost_or_limit: An inapposite-gate arrival can leave characters disoriented and poorly equipped for the location
the-strange.rule.translation-versus-goin.go_wrong: Abilities and gear may be inappropriate to the destination
the-strange.rule.translation-versus-goin.mind: An inapposite arrival can be disorienting
the-strange.rule.translation-versus-goin.blocked_reason: The rule describes travel and its consequences without requiring an unsupported effect.

the-strange.rule.routine-of-npcs-without.name: Routine of NPCs without the spark

effect.summary: An NPC without the spark follows a routine; interaction disrupts it temporarily before it eventually resumes.

the-strange.rule.routine-of-npcs-without.combines: PC interaction can interrupt the routine
the-strange.rule.routine-of-npcs-without.blocked_reason: A routine and its reset can be represented as ordinary game behavior.

the-strange.rule.vital-figures-and-recur.name: Vital figures and recursion nature

effect.summary: Figures central to a recursion may return after death or appear in an alternate recursion.

the-strange.rule.vital-figures-and-recur.cost_or_limit: They may be difficult to permanently remove
the-strange.rule.vital-figures-and-recur.who_may: Figures vital to a recursion’s identity
the-strange.rule.vital-figures-and-recur.combines: May recur in alternate versions of the setting
the-strange.rule.vital-figures-and-recur.blocked_reason: Returning after death or appearing in another recursion requires a death and persistence state beyond the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.recursion-size-and-conc.name: Recursion size and concept

effect.summary: A recursion is no larger than its concept, which may be as small as one room or street.

the-strange.rule.recursion-size-and-conc.cost_or_limit: The setting need not extend beyond its defining idea
the-strange.rule.recursion-size-and-conc.mind: Residents may believe an outside exists even when it does not
the-strange.rule.recursion-size-and-conc.combines: Can supply necessities without ordinary explanations
the-strange.rule.recursion-size-and-conc.blocked_reason: This is a setting constraint that can be adjudicated directly.

the-strange.rule.recursion-aging-and-rou.name: Recursion aging and routine

effect.summary: Recursion inhabitants may not age and may repeat the same actions over and over.

the-strange.rule.recursion-aging-and-rou.cost_or_limit: Depends on what suits the recursion
the-strange.rule.recursion-aging-and-rou.mind: Repeated behavior may resemble a rerun
the-strange.rule.recursion-aging-and-rou.mechanism: Time and behavior properties of a recursion
the-strange.rule.recursion-aging-and-rou.blocked_reason: The passage presents this as an optional world property.

the-strange.rule.psyche-exchange-in-the-.name: Psyche exchange in the urn chamber

effect.summary: A failed task exchanges a character’s psyche with that of a spirit in an urn.

the-strange.rule.psyche-exchange-in-the-.cost_or_limit: The exchange occurs on failure against difficulty 4.
the-strange.rule.psyche-exchange-in-the-.go_wrong: The spirit may impersonate the character and behave unpredictably.
the-strange.rule.psyche-exchange-in-the-.mind: The two psyches exchange bodies or identities.
the-strange.rule.psyche-exchange-in-the-.who_may: A character failing the task and an urn-bound spirit
the-strange.rule.psyche-exchange-in-the-.where_from: A trapped chamber lined with urns
the-strange.rule.psyche-exchange-in-the-.combines: The spirit is a psychopath from an earlier age.
the-strange.rule.psyche-exchange-in-the-.blocked_reason: The rule swaps a psyche with a trapped spirit.

the-strange.rule.questionable-vintage-ca.name: Questionable Vintage cask contents

effect.summary: Opening an intact cask produces a randomly determined effect, from explosion or poison to no effect or a temporary Edge increase.

the-strange.rule.questionable-vintage-ca.cost_or_limit: Roll a d20 per cask: results 1–5 explode for five fire and shrapnel damage; 6–8 contain level 5 poison; 9–14 have no effect; 15–17 grant +1 to an Edge for an hour; 18–20 grant +2 for an hour.
the-strange.rule.questionable-vintage-ca.go_wrong: Casks may explode or poison the drinker.
the-strange.rule.questionable-vintage-ca.who_may: Anyone opening a cask; the liquid affects its drinker
the-strange.rule.questionable-vintage-ca.combines: Contents are randomized by the roll.
the-strange.rule.questionable-vintage-ca.blocked_reason: The outcomes are discrete effects expressible with the basic grammar.

the-strange.rule.law-of-mad-science-or-m.name: Law of Mad Science or Magic

effect.summary: Allows zombie phenomena that would not normally occur under Standard Physics.

the-strange.rule.law-of-mad-science-or-m.cost_or_limit: Applies in the relevant Zed Omega recursions.
the-strange.rule.law-of-mad-science-or-m.who_may: Creatures and events in those recursions

the-strange.rule.cyphers-carry-between-r.name: Cyphers carry between recursions

effect.summary: Cyphers remain with a character when they translate, though their appearance may change.

the-strange.rule.cyphers-carry-between-r.cost_or_limit: Their appearance may change after translation.
the-strange.rule.cyphers-carry-between-r.blocked_reason: The passage gives an item-state change on translation, which the basic effect grammar does not represent.

the-strange.rule.focus-changes-on-transl.name: Focus changes on translation

effect.summary: On changing recursions, a character may exchange focus and its associated equipment, abilities, and skills.

the-strange.rule.focus-changes-on-transl.cost_or_limit: Changes depend on the new recursion and chosen focus.
the-strange.rule.focus-changes-on-transl.blocked_reason: The rule transfers or replaces a package of abilities and equipment when the character changes recursions.

the-strange.rule.cypher-single-use-effec.name: Cypher single-use effect

effect.summary: A cypher creates one often spectacular effect and is then spent.

the-strange.rule.cypher-single-use-effec.combines: Cyphers can reliably translate between recursions and to Earth
the-strange.rule.cypher-single-use-effec.blocked_reason: The rule describes a one-use effect.

the-strange.rule.cypher-proximity-cancel.name: Cypher proximity cancellation

effect.summary: Cyphers cancel each other when brought too close together.

the-strange.rule.cypher-proximity-cancel.cost_or_limit: Characters cannot carry many cyphers together
the-strange.rule.cypher-proximity-cancel.go_wrong: Cyphers gathered in one container cancel out
the-strange.rule.cypher-proximity-cancel.combines: Occultic cyphers count as two toward carrying capacity
the-strange.rule.cypher-proximity-cancel.blocked_reason: The passage gives no way to represent item-to-item proximity and cancellation in the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.occultic-cypher-carryin.name: Occultic cypher carrying limit

effect.summary: An occultic cypher counts as two cyphers for carrying capacity.

the-strange.rule.occultic-cypher-carryin.cost_or_limit: Each occultic cypher uses two carrying slots
the-strange.rule.occultic-cypher-carryin.go_wrong: Occultic cyphers are described as more dangerous
the-strange.rule.occultic-cypher-carryin.combines: Occultic cyphers are complex and often have stronger effects
the-strange.rule.occultic-cypher-carryin.blocked_reason: The passage does not give a basic-grammar mechanism for item carrying capacity.

the-strange.rule.edge-reduces-activation.name: Edge reduces activation costs

effect.summary: A stat's Edge reduces costs paid from that same stat Pool, potentially making an ability free.

the-strange.rule.edge-reduces-activation.cost_or_limit: Edge does not reduce damage; it applies only to its matching Pool
the-strange.rule.edge-reduces-activation.combines: Effort and ability costs may draw on the same Pool
the-strange.rule.edge-reduces-activation.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward resource-cost adjustment.

the-strange.rule.effort-limit.name: Effort limit

effect.summary: A character's Effort score caps the total Effort levels used on a roll.

the-strange.rule.effort-limit.cost_or_limit: First-tier characters have Effort 1; the maximum rises with experience
the-strange.rule.effort-limit.combines: Levels can be split between attack difficulty and damage
the-strange.rule.effort-limit.blocked_reason: The rule is a direct limit on task modification.

the-strange.rule.effort-cost-and-edge.name: Effort cost and Edge

effect.summary: Effort lowers task difficulty and costs Pool points; the relevant Edge reduces that cost once per action.

the-strange.rule.effort-cost-and-edge.cost_or_limit: The passage illustrates a three-point first Effort level and two points for a second, reduced by Edge.
the-strange.rule.effort-cost-and-edge.combines: Effort can lower difficulty; Edge applies once per action.
the-strange.rule.effort-cost-and-edge.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure rather than a world mechanism.

the-strange.rule.tier-advancement.name: Tier advancement

effect.summary: After purchasing one of each of four ability benefits, a character advances to the next tier.

the-strange.rule.tier-advancement.cost_or_limit: Each benefit costs 4 XP; duplicate benefits cannot be purchased before all four kinds are acquired.
the-strange.rule.tier-advancement.combines: The four benefit kinds are stat increases, Edge, Effort, and skills or qualifying special options.
the-strange.rule.tier-advancement.blocked_reason: This is a progression procedure, not a world mechanism.

the-strange.rule.training-and-specializa.name: Training and specialization

effect.summary: Training lowers related task difficulty by one step; specialization lowers it by two, and further training does not improve it.

the-strange.rule.training-and-specializa.cost_or_limit: Specialization is the maximum benefit from repeated training.
the-strange.rule.training-and-specializa.combines: Attack and defense training generally requires type abilities or rare exceptions.
the-strange.rule.training-and-specializa.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure rather than a world mechanism.

the-strange.rule.focus-changes-between-r.name: Focus changes between recursions

effect.summary: A character's focus may change with the recursion, while descriptor and type remain the same.

the-strange.rule.focus-changes-between-r.cost_or_limit: A chosen focus stays fixed for that recursion; a new recursion may permit choosing another.
the-strange.rule.focus-changes-between-r.combines: Different recursions can restrict which focuses are available.
the-strange.rule.focus-changes-between-r.blocked_reason: This is a character-building procedure, not a world mechanism.

the-strange.rule.ability-pool-costs.name: Ability Pool costs

effect.summary: Special abilities usually spend points from a stat Pool, with the relevant Edge reducing the cost once per action.

the-strange.rule.ability-pool-costs.cost_or_limit: Some abilities allow extra points or Effort to improve their effect.
the-strange.rule.ability-pool-costs.combines: Ability costs and Effort costs share the once-per-action Edge limit.
the-strange.rule.ability-pool-costs.blocked_reason: This is a game-use procedure rather than a world mechanism.

the-strange.rule.action-and-enabler-dist.name: Action and enabler distinction

effect.summary: An action ability consumes an action, while an enabler modifies or accompanies other actions without being an action itself.

the-strange.rule.action-and-enabler-dist.cost_or_limit: The ability description identifies whether it is an action or an enabler.
the-strange.rule.action-and-enabler-dist.combines: Enablers may function constantly or as part of another action.
the-strange.rule.action-and-enabler-dist.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure rather than a world mechanism.

the-strange.rule.the-spark-and-self-awar.name: The spark and self-awareness

effect.summary: An inhabitant who gains self-awareness and free will gains the spark; without it, a being cannot understand the Strange or recursions.

the-strange.rule.the-spark-and-self-awar.cost_or_limit: On Earth every intelligent being has the spark; the proportion varies among recursions, and some have none.
the-strange.rule.the-spark-and-self-awar.mind: The spark is full self-awareness and awareness of one's place in the wider world.
the-strange.rule.the-spark-and-self-awar.who_may: Intelligent inhabitants of recursions may have or gain it; all player characters have it.
the-strange.rule.the-spark-and-self-awar.combines: The spark does not itself grant knowledge of the Strange.
the-strange.rule.the-spark-and-self-awar.mechanism: sentience and eligibility to comprehend the Strange
the-strange.rule.the-spark-and-self-awar.blocked_reason: The spark changes self-awareness and sentience, beyond the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.quickened-connection.name: Quickened connection

effect.summary: Quickened beings have a special connection to the Strange that permits extraordinary abilities and unaided translation.

the-strange.rule.quickened-connection.cost_or_limit: Quickened beings are rare and may be limited to Earth and nearby recursions; all player characters are quickened.
the-strange.rule.quickened-connection.go_wrong: The claimed distribution beyond Earth's nearby recursions is presented as theory.
the-strange.rule.quickened-connection.mind: Requires the spark as well as the special connection.
the-strange.rule.quickened-connection.where_from: A unique connection to the Strange
the-strange.rule.quickened-connection.combines: Enables paradox revisions, vector moves, spinner twists, and translation without a special object.
the-strange.rule.quickened-connection.mechanism: Strange connection granting abilities and translation
the-strange.rule.quickened-connection.blocked_reason: The rule grants access to multiple powers and unaided translation through a special connection not represented by the basic grammar.

the-strange.rule.draggable-foci.name: Draggable foci

effect.summary: On first translation, a character may choose a supported local focus instead of bringing a previous draggable focus.

the-strange.rule.draggable-foci.cost_or_limit: The previous focus must be draggable for it to be carried forward.
the-strange.rule.draggable-foci.who_may: Characters translating to a recursion for the first time.
the-strange.rule.draggable-foci.combines: Local recursion focus options affect the choice.
the-strange.rule.draggable-foci.blocked_reason: A character-choice rule that does not require a missing effect capability.

the-strange.rule.focus-equipment-and-app.name: Focus equipment and appearance on translation

effect.summary: On entering a new recursion, a character's appearance, equipment, and focus may change to fit that world.

the-strange.rule.focus-equipment-and-app.cost_or_limit: Underlying appearance is presumed similar unless the player specifies otherwise; a focus may explicitly change physical appearance.
the-strange.rule.focus-equipment-and-app.mind: Descriptor and type do not change.
the-strange.rule.focus-equipment-and-app.who_may: Characters translating to a new recursion.
the-strange.rule.focus-equipment-and-app.combines: Focus descriptions determine new equipment; gear is recontextualized when possible.
the-strange.rule.focus-equipment-and-app.blocked_reason: Translation may alter a character's physical appearance and equipment.

the-strange.rule.sinfire-containment.name: Sinfire containment

effect.summary: Lotan's sinfire is held at Ardeyn's core so it does not sicken people except those who journey to witness it.

the-strange.rule.sinfire-containment.cost_or_limit: Exposure is associated with a forbidden journey to the core
the-strange.rule.sinfire-containment.go_wrong: Exposure can cause sickness and nightmares
the-strange.rule.sinfire-containment.mind: Sinfire burns the mind as sin
the-strange.rule.sinfire-containment.combines: Sinfire can pass through rare wielders, burning them only partly
the-strange.rule.sinfire-containment.blocked_reason: A powerful persistent hazard is contained within a location and affects those entering it.

the-strange.rule.follower-replacement.name: Follower replacement

effect.summary: A dead follower can be replaced after at least two weeks and proper recruitment.

the-strange.rule.follower-replacement.cost_or_limit: Requires two weeks or more and recruitment
the-strange.rule.follower-replacement.combines: Applies to followers gained through leadership
the-strange.rule.follower-replacement.mechanism: Delayed replacement of an allied NPC
the-strange.rule.follower-replacement.blocked_reason: It describes a delay and recruitment requirement.

the-strange.rule.chrysalid.name: CHRYSALID

effect.summary: While transformed, Intellect spending is restricted, nearby living creatures become compulsive targets, and reverting causes a penalty.

the-strange.rule.chrysalid.cost_or_limit: Only spend Intellect to attempt reversion; the penalty lasts an hour or a day depending on whether a real enemy was defeated.
the-strange.rule.chrysalid.go_wrong: The user may attack allies or bystanders and suffers a roll penalty after reverting.
the-strange.rule.chrysalid.mind: Target choice is compelled toward the nearest, or largest, living creature in range.
the-strange.rule.chrysalid.blocked_reason: Compulsive target selection requires controlling the user’s choices.

the-strange.rule.equipment-translation.name: Equipment translation

effect.summary: Ordinary equipment is replaced with equivalent context-appropriate gear at a new recursion; cyphers and rare Strange-based artifacts can travel and adapt.

the-strange.rule.equipment-translation.cost_or_limit: Ordinary equipment does not travel; carried cyphers and rare qualifying artifacts are exceptions.
the-strange.rule.equipment-translation.go_wrong: A cypher may change form while retaining its effect.
the-strange.rule.equipment-translation.where_from: The nature of recursions and the Strange.
the-strange.rule.equipment-translation.combines: Recursion Treader permits one mundane item to translate in changed form.
the-strange.rule.equipment-translation.blocked_reason: The rule requires equipment to be replaced, retained, or transformed according to its connection to the Strange.

the-strange.rule.currency-exchange-in-re.name: Currency exchange in recursions

effect.summary: Societies generally have ways to exchange currencies, and translating characters may receive money appropriate to their destination.

the-strange.rule.currency-exchange-in-re.cost_or_limit: Destination funds depend on character type and focus.
the-strange.rule.currency-exchange-in-re.who_may: Characters using currency in a recursion.
the-strange.rule.currency-exchange-in-re.combines: Examples include bits in Ruk and crowns in Ardeyn.
the-strange.rule.currency-exchange-in-re.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward economic rule.

the-strange.rule.armor-stacking-and-wear.name: Armor stacking and wearing

effect.summary: Only one armor type may be worn, but Armor bonuses from different sources add together; armor costs Might hourly and reduces Speed while worn.

the-strange.rule.armor-stacking-and-wear.cost_or_limit: Armor penalties depend on light, medium, or heavy armor; Speed returns when armor is removed.
the-strange.rule.armor-stacking-and-wear.go_wrong: Wearing armor can be taxing for an unpracticed character.
the-strange.rule.armor-stacking-and-wear.combines: Armor bonuses from multiple sources stack; one armor type only.
the-strange.rule.armor-stacking-and-wear.blocked_reason: The rule specifies ordinary equipment limits, bonuses, and costs.

the-strange.rule.weapon-familiarity-and-.name: Weapon familiarity and damage classes

effect.summary: Unfamiliar weapons make attacks harder; light, medium, and heavy weapons deal 2, 4, and 6 damage respectively, with light weapons easing attacks.

the-strange.rule.weapon-familiarity-and-.cost_or_limit: Heavy weapons require two hands; Armor applies according to the normal attack rules.
the-strange.rule.weapon-familiarity-and-.go_wrong: Using a weapon without practice raises attack difficulty by one step.
the-strange.rule.weapon-familiarity-and-.combines: Weapon size determines damage and handling.
the-strange.rule.weapon-familiarity-and-.blocked_reason: The rule maps directly to attack difficulty, damage, and hand requirements.

the-strange.rule.recursion-key-crafting.name: Recursion key crafting

effect.summary: A studied location can be opened by a key crafted over at least a week, with an XP cost and a level-based test.

the-strange.rule.recursion-key-crafting.cost_or_limit: The maker must be quickened, study the location for a day, spend a week crafting, and spend 1 XP.
the-strange.rule.recursion-key-crafting.go_wrong: Failure permits a retry, which requires Effort.
the-strange.rule.recursion-key-crafting.who_may: A quickened character who has studied the location.
the-strange.rule.recursion-key-crafting.combines: Uses ordinary crafting, building, and repair rules.
the-strange.rule.recursion-key-crafting.blocked_reason: This is a crafting cost and test that can be resolved with basic game procedures.

the-strange.rule.translation-strain.name: Translation strain

effect.summary: Repeated translation attempts in a day increase their difficulty for the whole group.

the-strange.rule.translation-strain.cost_or_limit: Each participant’s translation initiation, easing, hastening, or assistance within 24 hours adds one difficulty step to later attempts.
the-strange.rule.translation-strain.go_wrong: Penalties accumulate across participants and attempts.
the-strange.rule.translation-strain.who_may: Anyone attempting or helping with translation.
the-strange.rule.translation-strain.combines: Counts the whole group’s recent participation.
the-strange.rule.translation-strain.blocked_reason: A cumulative difficulty modifier is supported by the basic rules.

the-strange.rule.cyphers-carry-over.name: Cyphers carry over

effect.summary: A character’s cyphers remain with them when changing recursions, though their appearance may change.

the-strange.rule.cyphers-carry-over.cost_or_limit: Their new appearance should be noted after translation.
the-strange.rule.cyphers-carry-over.who_may: Characters translating to a new recursion.
the-strange.rule.cyphers-carry-over.combines: Items persist while their appearance may vary.
the-strange.rule.cyphers-carry-over.blocked_reason: The rule directly describes carried items and their altered appearance.

the-strange.rule.focus-changes-across-re.name: Focus changes across recursions

effect.summary: When changing recursions, a character’s clothing, belongings, and focus may change.

the-strange.rule.focus-changes-across-re.cost_or_limit: A draggable focus may be an exception; new focus benefits should be recorded.
the-strange.rule.focus-changes-across-re.combines: Can change appearance, skills, abilities, and equipment.
the-strange.rule.focus-changes-across-re.blocked_reason: The rule includes changes to a character’s appearance and form.

the-strange.rule.no-multiple-parallel-wo.name: No multiple parallel worlds

effect.summary: Recursions do not naturally create alternate selves or branching timelines.

the-strange.rule.no-multiple-parallel-wo.combines: Time-travel-themed recursions can imitate time travel.
the-strange.rule.no-multiple-parallel-wo.blocked_reason: This is a world restriction, not an unimplemented effect.

the-strange.rule.narratively-closed-recu.name: Narratively closed recursions

effect.summary: In some recursions natives follow their source fiction and lack the spark of self-awareness.

the-strange.rule.narratively-closed-recu.cost_or_limit: Natives generally do not recognize their world's limits or imagine travel beyond its story.
the-strange.rule.narratively-closed-recu.where_from: The nature of some fiction-seeded recursions.
the-strange.rule.narratively-closed-recu.blocked_reason: The rule describes a world constraint.

the-strange.rule.narrative-drift-and-sna.name: Narrative drift and snapback

effect.summary: Sparked populations can drive a recursion away from its source story, while major events can sometimes pull it closer again.

the-strange.rule.narrative-drift-and-sna.cost_or_limit: Snapback is possible below roughly thirty percent spark prevalence and becomes very difficult above that.
the-strange.rule.narrative-drift-and-sna.go_wrong: A sufficiently developed recursion may instead split into a separate world.
the-strange.rule.narrative-drift-and-sna.who_may: Applies to some recursions seeded from multiple stories.
the-strange.rule.narrative-drift-and-sna.where_from: The interaction of spark and fictional narratives.
the-strange.rule.narrative-drift-and-sna.combines: Key quests, deaths, or apparent destruction may trigger snapback.
the-strange.rule.narrative-drift-and-sna.blocked_reason: The grammar lacks a way to model world-scale narrative drift and fission.

the-strange.rule.the-strange-hosts-recur.name: The Strange hosts recursions

effect.summary: The Strange can host vast quantities of information, including fiction-seeded limited worlds.

the-strange.rule.the-strange-hosts-recur.cost_or_limit: The Strange is immense and continually expanding.
the-strange.rule.the-strange-hosts-recur.go_wrong: Its alien builders lost control of it and were killed or consumed.
the-strange.rule.the-strange-hosts-recur.who_may: Recursions arise from human fiction within the Strange.
the-strange.rule.the-strange-hosts-recur.where_from: An ancient alien data network in the dark-energy web.

the-strange.rule.standard-physics-compat.name: Standard Physics compatibility

effect.summary: Standard Physics artifacts can work in Magic, Mad Science, or Psionics recursions unless baseline physics is excluded.

the-strange.rule.standard-physics-compat.cost_or_limit: They must arrive through an inapposite gate.
the-strange.rule.standard-physics-compat.who_may: Standard Physics artifacts and their users.
the-strange.rule.standard-physics-compat.where_from: The interaction of recursion laws and matter gates.
the-strange.rule.standard-physics-compat.combines: Magic, Mad Science, and Psionics can retain an underlying Standard Physics framework.
the-strange.rule.standard-physics-compat.blocked_reason: This is a direct compatibility rule.

the-strange.rule.substandard-physics-res.name: Substandard Physics restriction

effect.summary: Substandard Physics recursions prevent Standard Physics-derived technology from functioning.

the-strange.rule.substandard-physics-res.cost_or_limit: Applies by definition in such recursions.

the-strange.rule.old-recursion-decline.name: Old recursion decline

effect.summary: Older recursions may become smaller, less sparked, or harder to reach as their source fictions fade from attention.

the-strange.rule.old-recursion-decline.cost_or_limit: Presented as competing hypotheses, not settled fact.
the-strange.rule.old-recursion-decline.go_wrong: Recursions may drift away or be negatively affected.
the-strange.rule.old-recursion-decline.where_from: Changing attention to their source stories.
the-strange.rule.old-recursion-decline.blocked_reason: The grammar does not model a world becoming less accessible or losing narrative presence.

the-strange.rule.recursion-edges.name: Recursion edges

effect.summary: A recursion's limits can loop paths, misdirect travelers, prolong travel, fade into outlines, or border the Strange.

the-strange.rule.recursion-edges.cost_or_limit: All recursions are limited, but their edges vary by context.
the-strange.rule.recursion-edges.go_wrong: Travelers may become lost or be translated elsewhere.
the-strange.rule.recursion-edges.who_may: Travelers who reach a recursion's edge.
the-strange.rule.recursion-edges.combines: Edges may appear as mist, looping routes, endless-looking terrain, or an abyss.
the-strange.rule.recursion-edges.blocked_reason: The described movement and concealment can be handled by the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.hazards-of-exposure.name: Hazards of exposure

effect.summary: Desert heat, dehydration, and airborne glass particles damage exposed travelers.

the-strange.rule.hazards-of-exposure.cost_or_limit: After an active day hour without about 0.2 liters of water, a traveler loses 2 Speed points per hour; every ten active hours causes 1 ambient damage.
the-strange.rule.hazards-of-exposure.go_wrong: Winds can create a sandstorm that causes 1 Speed damage per minute without shelter and reduces visibility to immediate range.
the-strange.rule.hazards-of-exposure.who_may: Travelers in the Glass Desert; those not needing water are exempt from dehydration.
the-strange.rule.hazards-of-exposure.where_from: The Glass Desert's heat, dryness, and abrasive glass sand.
the-strange.rule.hazards-of-exposure.combines: The Abides in Stone focus or similar water independence avoids dehydration.
the-strange.rule.hazards-of-exposure.blocked_reason: The stated damage and environmental restrictions fit the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.recursion-level-and-tra.name: Recursion level and translation difficulty

effect.summary: A recursion's level may make translation into it more or less difficult and is associated with its materials and inhabitants.

the-strange.rule.recursion-level-and-tra.cost_or_limit: The relationship can vary unless otherwise specified.
the-strange.rule.recursion-level-and-tra.blocked_reason: A world rule about translation and recursion properties.

the-strange.rule.recursion-native-skills.name: Recursion-native skills

effect.summary: Natives may know local skills; a translating character usually cannot acquire one through translation unless a focus grants it.

the-strange.rule.recursion-native-skills.cost_or_limit: A character may learn such skills through normal tier advancement.
the-strange.rule.recursion-native-skills.who_may: Recursion natives and visiting player characters.
the-strange.rule.recursion-native-skills.combines: A chosen focus may grant a local skill.

the-strange.rule.connection-to-the-stran.name: Connection to the Strange

effect.summary: Most recursions can serve as gateways into the Strange.

the-strange.rule.connection-to-the-stran.cost_or_limit: The form of the connection varies by recursion.
the-strange.rule.connection-to-the-stran.blocked_reason: A general setting mechanism for access to the Strange.

the-strange.rule.connection-to-earth.name: Connection to Earth

effect.summary: Every recursion is connected somehow to a prime world, usually Earth.

the-strange.rule.connection-to-earth.cost_or_limit: The manner of connection varies by recursion.
the-strange.rule.connection-to-earth.combines: Every recursion is hosted by the Strange.
the-strange.rule.connection-to-earth.blocked_reason: A general setting mechanism for access to a prime world.

the-strange.rule.the-spark.name: The spark

effect.summary: A recursion records the percentage of inhabitants who possess the spark.

the-strange.rule.the-spark.blocked_reason: A setting statistic rather than an unresolved effect.

the-strange.rule.honorable.name: Honorable

effect.summary: After a truly honorable act, the creature's next suitable task within an hour has its difficulty reduced by one step.

the-strange.rule.honorable.cost_or_limit: The act must be judged truly honorable, and the next task must not contradict it.
the-strange.rule.honorable.who_may: A creature acting honorably in a recursion with this trait.
the-strange.rule.honorable.where_from: A recursion with the Honorable trait.
the-strange.rule.honorable.combines: The modification applies to the creature's next task.
the-strange.rule.honorable.blocked_reason: A triggered, temporary task modifier can be run with the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.intelligent.name: Intelligent

effect.summary: A creature with the spark gains one maximum Intellect Pool point while in Atlantis and loses it on departure.

the-strange.rule.intelligent.cost_or_limit: Only spark-bearing creatures benefit, and only while in the recursion.
the-strange.rule.intelligent.go_wrong: The bonus ends when leaving Atlantis.
the-strange.rule.intelligent.who_may: Creatures with the spark in Atlantis.
the-strange.rule.intelligent.mechanism: Temporary attribute-capacity modifier tied to location.

the-strange.rule.atlantis-seeding.name: Atlantis seeding

effect.summary: Earth stories about Alumust's activities shaped the Strange cyst into a recursion resembling the Atlantis myth.

the-strange.rule.atlantis-seeding.cost_or_limit: The process unfolded over thousands of years.
the-strange.rule.atlantis-seeding.who_may: Fictional leakage and the Strange cyst are involved.
the-strange.rule.atlantis-seeding.combines: The recursion formed through feedback between myth and its source.
the-strange.rule.atlantis-seeding.mechanism: Fictional leakage reshapes a Strange cyst into a recursion.
the-strange.rule.atlantis-seeding.blocked_reason: A setting-history mechanism rather than a character effect.

the-strange.rule.brash.name: Brash

effect.summary: For a spark-bearing creature, attempts to resist or overcome fear or intimidation are one step easier.

the-strange.rule.brash.cost_or_limit: Applies to fear- or intimidation-related attempts in Camelot Le Morte.
the-strange.rule.brash.who_may: Creatures with the spark in Camelot Le Morte.
the-strange.rule.brash.blocked_reason: A task modifier can be run with the basic effect grammar.

the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.name: Mécanisme infection directive

effect.summary: A fully converted victim usually receives a rooted directive transferring loyalty to Gwenhwyfar's command module.

the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.cost_or_limit: The directive is level 4; conversion may also diminish the victim's mind.
the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.go_wrong: The victim may lose much of their former personality.
the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.mind: Binds loyalty to the command module in Gwenhwyfar.
