the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.who_may: Creatures converted by the maladie de la machine.
the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.where_from: The infection in Camelot Le Morte.
the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.combines: Mordred's protective magic can prevent or hold back infection.
the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.mechanism: Infection-triggered mental binding and allegiance change.
the-strange.rule.m-canisme-infection-dir.blocked_reason: The rule installs a persistent controlling directive in an infected creature's mind.

the-strange.rule.halloween-accords.name: Halloween Accords

effect.summary: Agreements among neighborhood rulers define borders and give trick-or-treaters protected status.

the-strange.rule.halloween-accords.cost_or_limit: Applies among Powers of the Night
the-strange.rule.halloween-accords.go_wrong: Breaking the agreements risks bloody chaos
the-strange.rule.halloween-accords.combines: Codified in scrolls held by several Powers
the-strange.rule.halloween-accords.blocked_reason: The passage says the Accords establish protected status and boundaries but does not define enforceable game mechanics.

the-strange.rule.currency-in-individual-.name: currency in individual pieces of wrapped hard candy

effect.summary: Halloween counts its currency as individual wrapped pieces of hard candy.

the-strange.rule.currency-in-individual-.cost_or_limit: Candy pieces are the unit of currency
the-strange.rule.currency-in-individual-.combines: Trick-or-treaters may earn candy through successful tricks
the-strange.rule.currency-in-individual-.blocked_reason: This rule is a simple setting convention.

the-strange.rule.one-minute.name: One minute

effect.summary: Things made by the Dragon Pen remain real for one minute.

the-strange.rule.one-minute.go_wrong: The created thing ceases to be real afterward
the-strange.rule.one-minute.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward duration limit.

the-strange.rule.a-drinker-is-not-made-i.name: A drinker is not made immortal

effect.summary: The Camelot Grail reverses age-related decline but does not prevent later normal aging or grant immortality.

the-strange.rule.a-drinker-is-not-made-i.cost_or_limit: Normal aging resumes; immortality is not granted
the-strange.rule.a-drinker-is-not-made-i.who_may: Anyone who drinks from the Holy Grail
the-strange.rule.a-drinker-is-not-made-i.combines: Applies to the Holy Grail’s healing effect
the-strange.rule.a-drinker-is-not-made-i.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward limitation on an artifact effect.

the-strange.rule.a-depleted-holy-grail-d.name: A depleted Holy Grail disappears

effect.summary: When depleted, the Grail vanishes and returns only after a successful quest to find it.

the-strange.rule.a-depleted-holy-grail-d.cost_or_limit: Requires a successful quest to restore it
the-strange.rule.a-depleted-holy-grail-d.blocked_reason: The rule changes an item’s existence and restoration state.

the-strange.rule.ascension.name: Ascension

effect.summary: A process turns high-ranking officers into undead cyborg Übermensch.

the-strange.rule.ascension.cost_or_limit: Requires science and magical relic cooperation
the-strange.rule.ascension.go_wrong: Earlier attempts could not reliably preserve lifespan, strength, resilience, and an intact mind
the-strange.rule.ascension.mind: An intact mind is a desired but difficult outcome
the-strange.rule.ascension.combines: Wissenschaftsbüro research and Schule der Archäologie relics
the-strange.rule.ascension.blocked_reason: Ascension changes an individual’s living and undead state, with survival and mind preservation concerns.

the-strange.rule.holy-grail-makes-unprep.name: Holy Grail makes unprepared drinkers zombies

effect.summary: Without implanted technological adjuvants, drinking the Reich’s Grail turns a person into a zombie.

the-strange.rule.holy-grail-makes-unprep.cost_or_limit: Requires surgical wiring, resistors, and related technology to avoid the result
the-strange.rule.holy-grail-makes-unprep.mind: The zombie outcome implies loss of ordinary personhood
the-strange.rule.holy-grail-makes-unprep.combines: Preparation is supplied by the Wissenschaftsbüro
the-strange.rule.holy-grail-makes-unprep.blocked_reason: The relic transforms drinkers into zombies.

the-strange.rule.trick-or-treaters-prote.name: Trick-or-treaters’ protected status

effect.summary: The Halloween Accords grant trick-or-treaters a special protected status.

the-strange.rule.trick-or-treaters-prote.cost_or_limit: Applies to trick-or-treaters under the Accords
the-strange.rule.trick-or-treaters-prote.combines: Observed by most Powers of the Night
the-strange.rule.trick-or-treaters-prote.mechanism: Protected status under a setting agreement
the-strange.rule.trick-or-treaters-prote.blocked_reason: The passage names a protected status but does not explain how it prevents harm or is enforced.

the-strange.rule.dispute-resolution.name: Dispute Resolution

effect.summary: Powers arbitrate disputes at the Midnight Circus every eleven nights; a champion fight may decide a case.

the-strange.rule.dispute-resolution.cost_or_limit: Meetings occur every eleven nights; Trial by Monster is a fight to the death.
the-strange.rule.dispute-resolution.blocked_reason: The rule is playable as stated.

the-strange.rule.sanctity-of-trick-or-tr.name: Sanctity of Trick-or-Treaters

effect.summary: Trick-or-treaters have protected status while following three rules on their rounds.

the-strange.rule.sanctity-of-trick-or-tr.cost_or_limit: Eating or using offered gifts, misusing a lit candle, or being caught in a prank, theft, or trespass removes protection for one night.
the-strange.rule.sanctity-of-trick-or-tr.go_wrong: Breaking a rule makes them viable prey.
the-strange.rule.sanctity-of-trick-or-tr.who_may: Trick-or-treaters who took the Vow of Begging.
the-strange.rule.sanctity-of-trick-or-tr.combines: Powers may impose consequences when protection is lost.
the-strange.rule.sanctity-of-trick-or-tr.blocked_reason: The protection and its conditions can be implemented as a rule.

the-strange.rule.vow-of-begging.name: Vow of Begging

effect.summary: A Halloween native can identify a trick-or-treater’s essence by studying them within immediate range for an action.

the-strange.rule.vow-of-begging.cost_or_limit: Requires an action and immediate range.
the-strange.rule.vow-of-begging.who_may: Trick-or-treaters who make the vow; other Halloween natives can sense its mark.
the-strange.rule.vow-of-begging.combines: Provides the identifiable essence used to recognize protected trick-or-treaters.
the-strange.rule.vow-of-begging.blocked_reason: A short-range sensing effect is supported.

the-strange.rule.geas.name: Geas

effect.summary: Magically obliges someone to perform a task or quest for the setter.

the-strange.rule.geas.cost_or_limit: The subject can temporarily escape by translating to a recursion without the law of Magic.
the-strange.rule.geas.mind: Compels the subject to fulfill an obligation.
the-strange.rule.geas.who_may: A subject targeted by whoever sets the geas.
the-strange.rule.geas.combines: Its operation can be escaped by translation to a recursion without the law of Magic.
the-strange.rule.geas.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar does not model a magically binding obligation or compulsion.

the-strange.rule.halloween-death-and-spi.name: Halloween death and spirits

effect.summary: Anyone killed in Halloween continues to exist as a spirit and is drawn to the Graveyard.

the-strange.rule.halloween-death-and-spi.cost_or_limit: A spirit may find peace if its remains are interred in the Graveyard and decompose naturally.
the-strange.rule.halloween-death-and-spi.go_wrong: Ghouls dig up about one in ten fresh graves.
the-strange.rule.halloween-death-and-spi.who_may: Anyone killed in Halloween, including visitors from other recursions.
the-strange.rule.halloween-death-and-spi.combines: Ghouls disturb graves and keep spirits plentiful.
the-strange.rule.halloween-death-and-spi.mechanism: Post-death spirit state and possible release.
the-strange.rule.halloween-death-and-spi.blocked_reason: Continuing existence as a spirit and achieving peace after death require soul-state mechanics.

the-strange.rule.mesozoica-time-temple-e.name: Mesozoica time temple effect

effect.summary: Entering the temple’s radiance can age a victim, remove them temporarily, or devolve their form; a successful defense grants limited local time travel.

the-strange.rule.mesozoica-time-temple-e.cost_or_limit: Failed difficulty 3 Intellect defense causes a GM-chosen effect; a successful victim may take up to three willing allies to an overlapping point in their own presence.
the-strange.rule.mesozoica-time-temple-e.go_wrong: If a time traveler’s original self becomes aware of them, one is randomly annihilated and the survivor may be trapped in a sealed loop.
the-strange.rule.mesozoica-time-temple-e.who_may: Anyone entering the temple’s radiance; successful subjects gain time mastery.
the-strange.rule.mesozoica-time-temple-e.mechanism: Time displacement, branching self interaction, and temporal hazards.
the-strange.rule.mesozoica-time-temple-e.blocked_reason: Time travel, overlapping selves, and sealed temporal loops require temporal mechanics beyond the basic grammar.

the-strange.rule.microcosmica-scale-on-t.name: Microcosmica scale on translation

effect.summary: Visitors to Microcosmica become approximately bacterium-sized; translation back out restores their normal size.

the-strange.rule.microcosmica-scale-on-t.cost_or_limit: Leaving by an inapposite gate preserves bacterial size until the traveler translates to another recursion.
the-strange.rule.microcosmica-scale-on-t.go_wrong: A bacterially sized traveler may be unable to interact with most things in the destination recursion.
the-strange.rule.microcosmica-scale-on-t.combines: Translation resets size; inapposite travel does not.
the-strange.rule.microcosmica-scale-on-t.blocked_reason: The rule changes a traveler’s physical scale and mass during dimensional travel.

the-strange.rule.microcosmica-return-loc.name: Microcosmica return location

effect.summary: A traveler who translates away returns to the same departure location if they translate back.

the-strange.rule.microcosmica-return-loc.cost_or_limit: Leave from Nereus One or another habitat able to support human life.
the-strange.rule.microcosmica-return-loc.go_wrong: Returning to an unprotected location can leave the traveler helpless in Microcosmica’s fluid-filled cavities.
the-strange.rule.microcosmica-return-loc.who_may: Travelers translating out of Microcosmica and back.
the-strange.rule.microcosmica-return-loc.combines: Translation is the safe way to leave.
the-strange.rule.microcosmica-return-loc.blocked_reason: The rule can be implemented as a fixed return position.

the-strange.rule.immunesuppres.name: ImmuneSuppres

effect.summary: Daily injections suppress harmful reactions to the quantum miniaturization context.

the-strange.rule.immunesuppres.cost_or_limit: Visitors staying longer than a day need daily injections.
the-strange.rule.immunesuppres.go_wrong: Without treatment, skin discolors and swells, then the subject declines and may die and decay.
the-strange.rule.immunesuppres.who_may: Researchers and recursors staying in Microcosmica.
the-strange.rule.immunesuppres.combines: Required for extended stays in Microcosmica.
the-strange.rule.immunesuppres.mechanism: Daily prophylaxis against contextual biological damage.
the-strange.rule.immunesuppres.blocked_reason: The progressive untreated deterioration and death require a disease or damage-over-time rule.

the-strange.rule.new-centropolis-vigilan.name: New Centropolis vigilante review

effect.summary: The DSA reviews superhuman incidents; public-good actions are accepted, while questionable or illegal acts can lead to arrest warrants and bounties.

the-strange.rule.new-centropolis-vigilan.cost_or_limit: Applies to superhuman activity in the recursion.
the-strange.rule.new-centropolis-vigilan.go_wrong: A superhuman judged to have acted unlawfully may be arrested.

the-strange.rule.recursion-native-reassi.name: recursion-native reassignment

effect.summary: Native researchers may be reassigned or retrieved by their university; a native with the spark can fear that recall will end their existence.

the-strange.rule.recursion-native-reassi.cost_or_limit: The passage presents this as the natives' limited existence beyond their recursion's narrative.
the-strange.rule.recursion-native-reassi.go_wrong: Recall may mean the end of a native's existence.
the-strange.rule.recursion-native-reassi.mind: A spark-bearing native may fear reassignment.
the-strange.rule.recursion-native-reassi.who_may: Recursion natives and their university department
the-strange.rule.recursion-native-reassi.blocked_reason: The rule concerns whether a recalled native continues to exist, a soul or existence state not represented by the basic grammar.

the-strange.rule.translation-during-tran.name: translation during transformation

effect.summary: Translating before transformation finishes saves the recursor's memories and restores a form fitting the new recursion.

the-strange.rule.translation-during-tran.cost_or_limit: Translation must happen before the twelve-hour transformation completes.
the-strange.rule.translation-during-tran.go_wrong: Waiting too long causes permanent loss of former memories.
the-strange.rule.translation-during-tran.mind: Memories survive only if translation occurs in time.
the-strange.rule.translation-during-tran.where_from: Recursion translation rules described for Microcosmica
the-strange.rule.translation-during-tran.combines: Interacts with the DNA injector's Transformation effect.
the-strange.rule.translation-during-tran.blocked_reason: It specifies persistence of identity and memory across bodily transformation and translation.

effect.summary: Earth's greys are genetically engineered hybrids with modified human DNA, designed to thrive on Earth.
The Mothership creates colonists when they are needed.

the-strange.rule.mothership-is-not-quick.name: Mothership is not quickened

effect.summary: The Mothership and Directorate are not quickened and are unlikely to have the spark.

the-strange.rule.mothership-is-not-quick.go_wrong: If the ship became quickened and entered the Strange, it might seek to colonize Earth.

the-strange.rule.oceanmist-cyphers-wash-.name: Oceanmist cyphers wash ashore

effect.summary: New cyphers wash onto Oceanmist's beach every few days.

the-strange.rule.oceanmist-cyphers-wash-.cost_or_limit: A maximum of seven appear each week, regardless of how many searchers there are.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-cyphers-wash-.who_may: Beachcombers can find them with a difficulty 6 Intellect roll per hour.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-cyphers-wash-.combines: Search success discovers a random cypher.

the-strange.rule.oceanmist-phase-change.name: Oceanmist phase change

effect.summary: The recursion changed from having no sparked natives to roughly one in twenty.

the-strange.rule.oceanmist-phase-change.cost_or_limit: Recent recursor visits and interactions likely catalyzed it.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-phase-change.go_wrong: The change brought greater danger and growth.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-phase-change.combines: New homes and inhabitants can be drawn into existence as the recursion grows.

the-strange.rule.oceanmist-natives-retur.name: Oceanmist natives return from death

effect.summary: Before the phase change, dead soldiers and sailors invariably returned; whether that still applies is uncertain.

the-strange.rule.oceanmist-natives-retur.cost_or_limit: The former return was required by the recursion's narrative.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-natives-retur.go_wrong: The changed recursion may no longer restore the dead.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-natives-retur.combines: The phase change may have altered this rule.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-natives-retur.blocked_reason: The passage describes whether dead people return to life.

the-strange.rule.oceanmist-growth.name: Oceanmist growth

effect.summary: When natives need homes, the growing recursion brings those places into existence with their staff.

the-strange.rule.oceanmist-growth.cost_or_limit: Further growth may follow increased popularity or the dragon gaining the spark.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-growth.where_from: The recursion's growth after its phase change.
the-strange.rule.oceanmist-growth.combines: Newly formed towers, castles, and ships arrive fully staffed.

the-strange.rule.r639-translation-diffic.name: R639 translation difficulty

effect.summary: Entering R639 is very difficult; attempts to leave are two steps harder, or three steps harder inside a reality scar.

the-strange.rule.r639-translation-diffic.cost_or_limit: Entry difficulty 10; exit difficulty gains two steps, or three within a scar.
the-strange.rule.r639-translation-diffic.go_wrong: A traveler may be unable to enter or leave.
the-strange.rule.r639-translation-diffic.combines: Reality scars add further travel difficulty.

the-strange.rule.r639-fear-trait.name: R639 fear trait

effect.summary: Fear, anxiety, and panic resistance tasks are one step harder throughout the recursion.

the-strange.rule.r639-fear-trait.go_wrong: Panicked characters may flee, freeze, faint, or scream; defense against the triggering creature becomes two steps harder.
the-strange.rule.r639-fear-trait.combines: Can compound fear during creature encounters.

the-strange.rule.r639-reality-scar-effec.name: R639 reality scar effects

effect.summary: A roughly 200-foot bubble distorts sight and sound, mutes some senses, raises task difficulty, and limits clear sight to immediate range.

the-strange.rule.r639-reality-scar-effec.cost_or_limit: Tasks are one step harder; imperfect outlines are visible to short range.
the-strange.rule.r639-reality-scar-effec.go_wrong: Incapacitation or severe shock can eject a visitor into a random Strange location, risking being lost.
the-strange.rule.r639-reality-scar-effec.mind: Sensory experience is dulled and distorted.
the-strange.rule.r639-reality-scar-effec.mechanism: area perception and difficulty field; forced spatial ejection
the-strange.rule.r639-reality-scar-effec.blocked_reason: It imposes a persistent area-wide field of sensory and task effects.

the-strange.rule.r639-pseudo-cypher-tran.name: R639 pseudo-cypher translation

effect.summary: A lump brought out of R639 becomes an identifiable cypher, which hatches into a killing white light after use.

the-strange.rule.r639-pseudo-cypher-tran.cost_or_limit: The lump must leave R639 or undergo its triggering event first.
the-strange.rule.r639-pseudo-cypher-tran.go_wrong: The used cypher becomes a creature instead of evaporating.
the-strange.rule.r639-pseudo-cypher-tran.combines: The resolved cypher functions normally before hatching.
the-strange.rule.r639-pseudo-cypher-tran.mechanism: item state transition and delayed creature release
the-strange.rule.r639-pseudo-cypher-tran.blocked_reason: The item has a conditional state change and later produces a creature.

the-strange.rule.r639-inapposite-gate-re.name: R639 inapposite gate recurrence

effect.summary: When one inapposite gate is destroyed, another forms at a random location a few months later.

the-strange.rule.r639-inapposite-gate-re.go_wrong: Destroying a gate does not permanently remove access.

the-strange.rule.r639-artifacts-rely-on-.name: R639 artifacts rely on its Exotic law

effect.summary: R639 artifacts function normally under other laws for only a few days.

the-strange.rule.r639-artifacts-rely-on-.cost_or_limit: Normal function elsewhere lasts a few days.
the-strange.rule.r639-artifacts-rely-on-.combines: Applies to the artifacts of R639.
the-strange.rule.r639-artifacts-rely-on-.blocked_reason: A duration limit on item operation is representable as a rule.

the-strange.rule.hyperspace-travel-links.name: Hyperspace travel links the planets

effect.summary: Travel between planets requires a starship with a hyperspace drive and takes a few hours; ships act as conduits between inaccessible regions.

the-strange.rule.hyperspace-travel-links.cost_or_limit: A hyperspace-drive starship is required; journeys take hours.
the-strange.rule.hyperspace-travel-links.who_may: Travelers with access to such a ship
the-strange.rule.hyperspace-travel-links.blocked_reason: The restriction and travel mechanism can be represented as a rule.

the-strange.rule.rebel-galaxy-is-far-sma.name: Rebel Galaxy is far smaller than its inhabitants believe

effect.summary: Each apparent planet is only a small area, with unseen space implied to repeat the same pattern.

the-strange.rule.rebel-galaxy-is-far-sma.mind: Inhabitants believe they live in a vast galaxy.
the-strange.rule.rebel-galaxy-is-far-sma.blocked_reason: This is a setting fact rather than an unrepresented game effect.

the-strange.rule.space-battle-targeting-.name: Space-battle targeting and coordination

effect.summary: Ship level differences and coordinated attacks modify roll difficulty; targeting systems adds difficulty in exchange for disabling them.

the-strange.rule.space-battle-targeting-.cost_or_limit: This is a game procedure for vehicle combat.
the-strange.rule.space-battle-targeting-.combines: Skill and Effort also modify rolls.
the-strange.rule.space-battle-targeting-.blocked_reason: It is game procedure, not a world-mechanism rule.

the-strange.rule.killarus-translation-wa.name: Killarus translation ward

effect.summary: Recursors can translate into Killarus but cannot translate out.

the-strange.rule.killarus-translation-wa.where_from: Killarus; installed by Zal with a powerful machine
the-strange.rule.killarus-translation-wa.blocked_reason: The grammar cannot represent a persistent, direction-specific barrier to translation.

the-strange.rule.moon-magic.name: Moon Magic

effect.summary: Magic works flawlessly about one day in four according to a shifting schedule set by the GM; related abilities and creatures are weak at other times.

the-strange.rule.moon-magic.cost_or_limit: Active days are difficult to predict; inactive focus use is one step harder.
the-strange.rule.moon-magic.go_wrong: Magic-related beings and powers become tentative, pale, and weak when inactive.
the-strange.rule.moon-magic.blocked_reason: The rule describes when a world law operates and its limitation.

the-strange.rule.hirotomo-returns-to-lif.name: Hirotomo returns to life

effect.summary: Karou Hirotomo returns to life a few days after being killed.

the-strange.rule.hirotomo-returns-to-lif.cost_or_limit: Return occurs after a few days.
the-strange.rule.hirotomo-returns-to-lif.combines: The Shogun has the same return-to-life trait.
the-strange.rule.hirotomo-returns-to-lif.blocked_reason: Returning after death requires representing a persistent post-death state and restoration.

the-strange.rule.the-shogun-returns-to-l.name: The Shogun returns to life

effect.summary: The Shogun returns to life a few days after being killed.

the-strange.rule.the-shogun-returns-to-l.cost_or_limit: Return occurs after a few days.
the-strange.rule.the-shogun-returns-to-l.blocked_reason: Returning after death requires representing a persistent post-death state and restoration.

the-strange.rule.shared-extra-lives.name: Shared extra lives

effect.summary: Deaths of Tokugawa and three companions consume a shared reserve of 101 lives before normal death resumes.

the-strange.rule.shared-extra-lives.cost_or_limit: A finite reserve of 101 lives for the four
the-strange.rule.shared-extra-lives.go_wrong: When exhausted, the original four die normally
the-strange.rule.shared-extra-lives.where_from: A rebounded oni spell infused their life force
the-strange.rule.shared-extra-lives.combines: Possibly caused by Tokugawa’s relic artifact
the-strange.rule.shared-extra-lives.blocked_reason: A shared pool of lives governing death and survival requires soul-state tracking.

the-strange.rule.moonstorm.name: Moonstorm

effect.summary: The moon’s phase is frozen, keeping Magic high and supernatural creatures active.

the-strange.rule.moonstorm.go_wrong: Oni, phantoms, and other creatures run wild
the-strange.rule.moonstorm.combines: Shogun seeks to restart the normal cycle
the-strange.rule.moonstorm.blocked_reason: An ongoing world-scale condition with broad consequences needs persistent state beyond a basic effect.

the-strange.rule.yobuko-mask-sight-and-h.name: Yobuko mask sight and hearing

effect.summary: A removed mask lets its owner sense the location where it is, while the owner’s body is effectively blind and deaf nearby.

the-strange.rule.yobuko-mask-sight-and-h.cost_or_limit: The mask can be stolen and locked away; the effect ends when retrieved
the-strange.rule.yobuko-mask-sight-and-h.go_wrong: A stolen mask can leave its owner unable to perceive around her body
the-strange.rule.yobuko-mask-sight-and-h.combines: Yobuko resist name magic by one defense step
the-strange.rule.yobuko-mask-sight-and-h.blocked_reason: Remote perception through a detached mask and linked sensory impairment require coupled effects.

the-strange.rule.cloud-sea-changing-loca.name: Cloud Sea changing locations

effect.summary: New creatures and places sometimes appear in the Cloud Sea without apparent cause.

the-strange.rule.cloud-sea-changing-loca.blocked_reason: Creating new locations and creatures unpredictably requires world-state generation beyond a basic effect.

the-strange.rule.library-book-availabili.name: Library book availability

effect.summary: A book published on Earth or the Shoals may have a copy in the Lost Stacks.

the-strange.rule.library-book-availabili.cost_or_limit: A copy is only potentially present
the-strange.rule.library-book-availabili.go_wrong: Finding a specific book may require days of research
the-strange.rule.library-book-availabili.combines: Books can contain information from other recursions
the-strange.rule.library-book-availabili.blocked_reason: The collection may include titles across worlds, requiring cross-world access rules.

the-strange.rule.master-librarian-s-mask.name: Master Librarian’s masks

effect.summary: The Master Librarian cannot be killed until all of his masks are destroyed.

the-strange.rule.master-librarian-s-mask.cost_or_limit: Every mask belonging to him must be destroyed
the-strange.rule.master-librarian-s-mask.combines: He hides spare masks around the Library
the-strange.rule.master-librarian-s-mask.blocked_reason: A creature’s survival tied to the state of multiple remote masks requires special state tracking.

the-strange.rule.book-bound-recursor-tra.name: Book-bound recursor translation

effect.summary: A bound recursor returns to normal when a third party translates the book out of Seishin Shore, but becomes a book again on return.

the-strange.rule.book-bound-recursor-tra.cost_or_limit: A third party must translate the bound book away
the-strange.rule.book-bound-recursor-tra.go_wrong: Returning to Seishin Shore restores the book state
the-strange.rule.book-bound-recursor-tra.mind: The book contains the creature’s knowledge
the-strange.rule.book-bound-recursor-tra.blocked_reason: Identity and form persist across translation and revert according to location.

the-strange.rule.sword-realms-translatio.name: Sword Realms translation difficulty

effect.summary: Translation difficulty depends on origin and destination.

the-strange.rule.sword-realms-translatio.cost_or_limit: Entering from Earth or an unaffiliated recursion is difficulty 6; moving between connected recursions is usually difficulty 3; translating out from within adds two difficulty steps.
the-strange.rule.sword-realms-translatio.combines: Some connected borders can be crossed simply by walking.

the-strange.rule.dead-spirits-and-abysm.name: Dead spirits and Abysm

effect.summary: Some dead spirits persist and may be drawn into Abysm.

the-strange.rule.dead-spirits-and-abysm.cost_or_limit: The outcome is uncertain for a recursor who dies in the Sword Realms.
the-strange.rule.dead-spirits-and-abysm.go_wrong: The dead may suffer torment in Abysm.
the-strange.rule.dead-spirits-and-abysm.who_may: Dead creatures and possibly dead recursors
the-strange.rule.dead-spirits-and-abysm.combines: Related to Abysm's inhabitants and its ruler Janus.
the-strange.rule.dead-spirits-and-abysm.blocked_reason: It requires representing souls that persist after death and can be transported to an afterlife.

the-strange.rule.sword-realms-phase-depe.name: Sword Realms phase-dependent access

effect.summary: Some known places cannot be reached until a suitable phase or other condition occurs.

the-strange.rule.sword-realms-phase-depe.cost_or_limit: A moon phase or another external ingredient may be required.
the-strange.rule.sword-realms-phase-depe.go_wrong: The location remains inaccessible until the condition is met.

the-strange.rule.gods-precipitate-into-e.name: Gods precipitate into existence

effect.summary: Pressing a recursion's boundaries can make a merely possible god real.

the-strange.rule.gods-precipitate-into-e.cost_or_limit: The risk comes from pushing a recursion's boundaries.
the-strange.rule.gods-precipitate-into-e.go_wrong: A powerful god may gain the spark and become real.
the-strange.rule.gods-precipitate-into-e.who_may: Anyone pushing a recursion's boundaries may trigger it.
the-strange.rule.gods-precipitate-into-e.combines: Potential gods may come from familiar fiction or religion.

the-strange.rule.slavery-sentence-and-ta.name: Slavery sentence and tattoo

effect.summary: A magical skin mark binds a sentenced slave only for the specified term, then vanishes.

the-strange.rule.slavery-sentence-and-ta.cost_or_limit: The service period is limited to the sentence's stated term.
the-strange.rule.slavery-sentence-and-ta.go_wrong: Extending the term or harming the slave is itself criminal.
the-strange.rule.slavery-sentence-and-ta.combines: The mark magically records and enforces the sentence duration.
the-strange.rule.slavery-sentence-and-ta.blocked_reason: The rule imposes a binding service relationship on a person.

the-strange.rule.gold-throne-reincarnati.name: Gold throne reincarnation

effect.summary: A reliquary wearer who is killed returns at full health the following round.

the-strange.rule.gold-throne-reincarnati.cost_or_limit: The charm works once; use can cause spiritual malaise.
the-strange.rule.gold-throne-reincarnati.go_wrong: A soul from Abysm may possess the revived person, causing pain or madness.
the-strange.rule.gold-throne-reincarnati.who_may: A wearer of a gold throne reliquary
the-strange.rule.gold-throne-reincarnati.combines: Malaise can require powerful magic or the Empress's permission to reverse.
the-strange.rule.gold-throne-reincarnati.blocked_reason: The revival may replace or share the wearer's identity with a soul from Abysm.

the-strange.rule.foldable-keep-contents.name: Foldable keep contents

effect.summary: When a keep folds, remaining occupants or foreign objects may be ejected or kept in stasis.

the-strange.rule.foldable-keep-contents.cost_or_limit: The particular keep determines which result occurs.
the-strange.rule.foldable-keep-contents.go_wrong: Occupants who fail to exit may be ejected or trapped in stasis.
the-strange.rule.foldable-keep-contents.who_may: Creatures and foreign objects inside a foldable keep
the-strange.rule.foldable-keep-contents.combines: Triggered by folding the keep back into its sheet form.
the-strange.rule.foldable-keep-contents.blocked_reason: The rule requires choosing between ejection and stasis for occupants or contents.

the-strange.rule.darkness-initiation.name: Darkness initiation

effect.summary: Those who fully join the Darkness become flesh-eating ghouls and cannot return.

the-strange.rule.darkness-initiation.go_wrong: The transformed person joins a corpse-feeding existence.
the-strange.rule.darkness-initiation.who_may: Those fully committing to the Darkness
the-strange.rule.darkness-initiation.blocked_reason: The rule requires permanently changing a character's body and creature type.

the-strange.rule.zed-america-quick-heali.name: Zed America quick healing

effect.summary: Everyone carries weak HRV, which adds one to recovery-roll results.

the-strange.rule.zed-america-quick-heali.cost_or_limit: Applies to everyone in Zed America.
the-strange.rule.zed-america-quick-heali.go_wrong: Virulent HRV can cause uncontrolled replication.
the-strange.rule.zed-america-quick-heali.blocked_reason: This rule is a straightforward modifier to recovery results.

the-strange.rule.hrv-infection-and-death.name: HRV infection and death

effect.summary: A zombie bite can infect a victim; active infection worsens their condition, and death while infected can lead to zombification.

the-strange.rule.hrv-infection-and-death.cost_or_limit: The victim first makes a Might defense within an hour of being bitten; active disease prompts another defense every 24 hours. Death may be followed by zombification in 1d6 hours, sometimes within an hour.
the-strange.rule.hrv-infection-and-death.go_wrong: A victim can become a zombie after failed defenses or death.
the-strange.rule.hrv-infection-and-death.mind: The converted person’s mind is burned out by hunger.
the-strange.rule.hrv-infection-and-death.who_may: People bitten by zombies or undergoing runaway HRV replication.
the-strange.rule.hrv-infection-and-death.combines: Weak native HRV can be triggered into replication by a bite.
the-strange.rule.hrv-infection-and-death.mechanism: Infection, progressive damage, and postmortem conversion.
the-strange.rule.hrv-infection-and-death.blocked_reason: The rule turns an infected human into a zombie, requiring a creature-form transformation.

the-strange.rule.blood-testing-in-zed-am.name: Blood testing in Zed America

effect.summary: A blood test measures HRV load; refusal is treated as a failed test.

the-strange.rule.blood-testing-in-zed-am.cost_or_limit: Testing is required for enclave entry, after zed contact, and at secure biolabs; authorities may demand it at their discretion.
the-strange.rule.blood-testing-in-zed-am.go_wrong: Failure can lead to expulsion or immediate euthanasia; drones attempt restraint.
the-strange.rule.blood-testing-in-zed-am.who_may: Drones, law enforcement, and enclave authorities administer or require tests.
the-strange.rule.blood-testing-in-zed-am.combines: People with Regenerates Tissue need a medical card to explain their HRV status.
the-strange.rule.blood-testing-in-zed-am.blocked_reason: The rule is a test with a threshold and defined consequences.

the-strange.rule.artifact-transfer-betwe.name: Artifact transfer between recursions

effect.summary: Artifacts can be transferred between recursions using gates, the Strange, abilities, cyphers, or other methods.

the-strange.rule.artifact-transfer-betwe.who_may: Recursion miners and other travelers with a method.
the-strange.rule.artifact-transfer-betwe.combines: Methods include inapposite gates and temporary gates.
the-strange.rule.artifact-transfer-betwe.blocked_reason: The rule describes ordinary transport by established travel methods.

the-strange.rule.flatland-s-peace-cry-la.name: Flatland’s peace-cry law

effect.summary: Women must sound a peace cry in public to avoid accidentally stabbing others.

the-strange.rule.flatland-s-peace-cry-la.cost_or_limit: Applies to women moving in public places.
the-strange.rule.flatland-s-peace-cry-la.blocked_reason: This is a social rule, not an unrepresentable power.

the-strange.rule.law-of-the-jungle.name: Law of the Jungle

effect.summary: Codes govern relations within and between animal packs and tribes and restrict killing humans.

the-strange.rule.law-of-the-jungle.cost_or_limit: Humans may be killed under limited exceptions, including sudden arrival as recursors.
the-strange.rule.law-of-the-jungle.go_wrong: Violators risk conflict with the community and Shere Khan.
the-strange.rule.law-of-the-jungle.who_may: Packs and tribes of the Kiplingverse.
the-strange.rule.law-of-the-jungle.combines: Baloo teaches and enforces it against the monkeys’ disregard.
the-strange.rule.law-of-the-jungle.blocked_reason: This is a world rule, not an unrepresentable power.

the-strange.rule.moonbase-tranquility-he.name: Moonbase Tranquility helium-3 deposit

effect.summary: Solar wind deposited helium-3 in the moon’s regolith over billions of years.

the-strange.rule.moonbase-tranquility-he.cost_or_limit: The deposit is mined by autonomous drones.
the-strange.rule.moonbase-tranquility-he.combines: The isotope is collected and stored in large magnetic tanks.
the-strange.rule.moonbase-tranquility-he.blocked_reason: A world mechanism, not an unsupported character effect.

the-strange.rule.bacterial-survival-on-l.name: Bacterial survival on lethal worlds

effect.summary: Ordinary humans may need protective suits to survive in Microcosmica, while bacterial characters can function there without one.

the-strange.rule.bacterial-survival-on-l.cost_or_limit: Without protection, most recursors suffocate and die almost immediately.
the-strange.rule.bacterial-survival-on-l.go_wrong: Unprotected characters die in the hostile environment.
the-strange.rule.bacterial-survival-on-l.combines: The Bacterial form provides an exception.
the-strange.rule.bacterial-survival-on-l.blocked_reason: This is a world rule that can be represented as environmental damage or protection.

the-strange.rule.samurai-stewardship.name: Samurai stewardship

effect.summary: A samurai serving a Karou receives stewardship of a holding, while a ronin does not receive that benefit automatically.

the-strange.rule.samurai-stewardship.cost_or_limit: The holder must manage staff and property or delegate the work.
the-strange.rule.samurai-stewardship.go_wrong: Neglecting management leaves the holder’s responsibilities unmet.
the-strange.rule.samurai-stewardship.who_may: Samurai in a Karou’s service; ronin may obtain property by other means.
the-strange.rule.samurai-stewardship.combines: Linked to service under a Karou.
the-strange.rule.samurai-stewardship.blocked_reason: The rule can be handled as an ordinary character benefit and responsibility.

the-strange.rule.spell-tattoo-collection.name: Spell Tattoo Collection

effect.summary: Only readied tattoo spells can be cast; changing one takes a minute, and selections can be varied twice daily after specified recovery rolls.

the-strange.rule.spell-tattoo-collection.cost_or_limit: One minute per switch; at most two selection changes per day, immediately after a one-hour or ten-hour recovery roll.
the-strange.rule.spell-tattoo-collection.who_may: Casters with Inks Spells on Skin.
the-strange.rule.spell-tattoo-collection.combines: Spells may be substituted from Casts Spells or learned from an artifact spellbook if allowed.
the-strange.rule.spell-tattoo-collection.blocked_reason: The rule restricts which tattoo-carried spells are available and how they can be changed.

the-strange.rule.blood-spellcasting-risk.name: Blood spellcasting risk

effect.summary: Using the caster’s blood may increase a spell’s power but risks the caster’s soul.

the-strange.rule.blood-spellcasting-risk.cost_or_limit: Uses the caster’s own blood; exact cost is unspecified.
the-strange.rule.blood-spellcasting-risk.go_wrong: The caster’s soul may be endangered.
the-strange.rule.blood-spellcasting-risk.who_may: A caster using their own blood to cast.
the-strange.rule.blood-spellcasting-risk.blocked_reason: The rule threatens the caster’s soul without specifying a basic-grammar effect.

the-strange.rule.suspended-animation-whi.name: Suspended animation while petrified

effect.summary: A living creature turned to stone is suspended; returning to flesh does not undo damage sustained while petrified.

the-strange.rule.suspended-animation-whi.cost_or_limit: Petrification must later be reversed for the creature to return to flesh.
the-strange.rule.suspended-animation-whi.go_wrong: Injuries during petrification may be disfiguring, debilitating, or fatal.
the-strange.rule.suspended-animation-whi.who_may: Living creatures magically turned to stone.
the-strange.rule.suspended-animation-whi.blocked_reason: The rule defines a creature’s state and survival across suspended animation.

the-strange.rule.halloween-accords-prote.name: Halloween Accords protections

effect.summary: Trick-or-treaters receive accord protections while following the rules, including carrying a lit candle and avoiding eating treats, trespass, and vandalism.

the-strange.rule.halloween-accords-prote.cost_or_limit: Protection depends on observance of the accords.
the-strange.rule.halloween-accords-prote.go_wrong: Breaking the conditions may forfeit the stated protections.
the-strange.rule.halloween-accords-prote.who_may: Trick-or-treaters in Halloween and similar recursions.
the-strange.rule.halloween-accords-prote.combines: The accords also define boundaries and lawful dispute resolution.
the-strange.rule.halloween-accords-prote.blocked_reason: The rule sets behavioral conditions for social protection.

the-strange.rule.mist-star-mount-protect.name: Mist star mount protects air-breathing rider

effect.summary: An air-breathing rider does not drown while mounted on an underwater-traveling mist star.

the-strange.rule.mist-star-mount-protect.cost_or_limit: Applies to a rider mounted on a mist star traveling underwater.
the-strange.rule.mist-star-mount-protect.blocked_reason: The protection can be represented as a straightforward effect.

the-strange.rule.death-in-the-glass-dese.name: Death in the Glass Desert can trap a spirit

effect.summary: A human or qephilim who dies in the Glass Desert has a chance of becoming a trapped sere spirit instead of reaching the Roads of Sorrow.

the-strange.rule.death-in-the-glass-dese.cost_or_limit: This happens only sometimes, rather than to every death there.
the-strange.rule.death-in-the-glass-dese.go_wrong: The trapped spirit may become slowly insane and furious.
the-strange.rule.death-in-the-glass-dese.mind: The spirit is exposed to its own reflected image and may lose its reason.
the-strange.rule.death-in-the-glass-dese.who_may: Humans and qephilim who die in the Glass Desert.
the-strange.rule.death-in-the-glass-dese.combines: The spirit can later be jolted back to consciousness when a living creature sees its reflection.
the-strange.rule.death-in-the-glass-dese.mechanism: Death can leave a soul trapped in a location rather than following its usual path.
the-strange.rule.death-in-the-glass-dese.blocked_reason: The rule requires a post-death spirit state and possible afterlife destination.

the-strange.rule.seeing-a-sere-spirit-s-.name: Seeing a sere spirit’s reflection wakes it

effect.summary: A living creature seeing the spirit’s reflection jolts it back to consciousness.

the-strange.rule.seeing-a-sere-spirit-s-.cost_or_limit: The trigger is seeing the reflection where none should be.
the-strange.rule.seeing-a-sere-spirit-s-.go_wrong: The spirit usually wakes in fury.
the-strange.rule.seeing-a-sere-spirit-s-.mind: The spirit returns to consciousness, often furious.
the-strange.rule.seeing-a-sere-spirit-s-.who_may: A living creature who sees the reflection triggers it.
the-strange.rule.seeing-a-sere-spirit-s-.where_from: A spirit trapped in reflective material.
the-strange.rule.seeing-a-sere-spirit-s-.combines: Waking lets the spirit see and attack the person who noticed it.
the-strange.rule.seeing-a-sere-spirit-s-.blocked_reason: The effect requires a trapped spirit to persist in an unconscious suspended state.

the-strange.rule.using-a-tetsu-tide-jewe.name: Using a tetsu tide jewel reveals an egg

effect.summary: Using a tide jewel to quell a storm or transfer someone reveals it as a tetsu egg, which hatches and releases a hatchling.

the-strange.rule.using-a-tetsu-tide-jewe.cost_or_limit: Triggered by either described use of the jewel.
the-strange.rule.using-a-tetsu-tide-jewe.go_wrong: The item hatches, releasing a tetsu hatchling.
the-strange.rule.using-a-tetsu-tide-jewe.who_may: Anyone who uses a tetsu tide jewel.
the-strange.rule.using-a-tetsu-tide-jewe.where_from: Tetsu eggs can take the apparent form of tide jewels.
the-strange.rule.using-a-tetsu-tide-jewe.combines: The jewel’s two powers trigger the same hatching outcome.
the-strange.rule.using-a-tetsu-tide-jewe.mechanism: A powered item is actually an egg that hatches when activated.
the-strange.rule.using-a-tetsu-tide-jewe.blocked_reason: The rule requires an item to carry powers whose use triggers its transformation and release of a creature.

the-strange.rule.zombie-lethal-attacks-d.name: Zombie lethal attacks depend on the attack roll

effect.summary: A hit that would reduce a sprayer, sprinter, or hulk to zero health does so only on an even roll; an odd roll leaves it at one health.

the-strange.rule.zombie-lethal-attacks-d.cost_or_limit: Applies to the specified zombie varieties when an attack would reduce them to zero health.
the-strange.rule.zombie-lethal-attacks-d.go_wrong: An odd roll prevents the apparent killing blow from being lethal.
the-strange.rule.zombie-lethal-attacks-d.who_may: Applies to zombie sprayers, sprinters, and hulks.
the-strange.rule.zombie-lethal-attacks-d.where_from: The zombie varieties described in the passage.
the-strange.rule.zombie-lethal-attacks-d.combines: The same rule applies to all three listed varieties.
the-strange.rule.zombie-lethal-attacks-d.mechanism: A parity check modifies whether an otherwise lethal attack kills.
the-strange.rule.zombie-lethal-attacks-d.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward conditional alteration of damage outcome.
